Before I start i will say that i intially say that i bought this game back in August 2015, and decided at the time that it was not for me and returned for a refund. I decided to give it another try, partially due to a prepaid gift card i got for Xmas and partly due to having just taken a very interesting class on World War I last semester at college.
There is so much to cover and i will likely miss quit a bit, so i highly recommend watching 'Lets Play' videos of this to get the idea. Also if you have specific questions, as i will miss alot, feel free to leave them in the comments of this review and i will answer as best i can, if i can.
I would definetly have to recommend this game. There are not alot of WWI games out there that are not flight simulators, and this one is simple enough to appeal to the masses and, i think, complex enough to not be considered "dumbed down"
The game is all played on one large map, which includes all of Europe to the Urals except for the northern parts of Scandinavia. The map also includes well as North Africa, The entire extent of the Ottoman Empire in the Middle East at the time, as well as Western Persia, and the Eastern seaboard of the US and Canada. The war was fought in other places, like East Africa, but the bulk of the fighting did occur within the area of this map, so it is acceptable.
Basically, you dont play as an individual nation, but as one of two sides:
the Triple Entente (Russia, France, Great Britian) and its Allies (Serbia, Italy, Portugal and others)
Or the Central Powers (Germany, Austria Hungary, The Ottoman Empire and others that may join)
All the nations not in the war at the time you are playing are grouped together as neutral nations. But nations can join the conflict on thier own or by you declaring war on them.
The game gives you five options of campaign:
1914: Basically the war starts the way it did, and you have until 1919 to achieve victory for your side, 118 turns max.
With this, you dont start with everything, you only start with the fighting between Serbia and Austria Hungary, then over a few turns, Germany attacking Belgium is added, then the Russian Attacks in the East.
NOTE: As of this writing i have only played one campaign, as the Entente from 1914, and won in 1917 in two long play sessions

The other scenarios start at the begining of thier respective years: 1915, 1916, 1917, 1918. but all must be concluded by 1919
In terms of difficutly, there are three options with regard to the AI that will oppose you: Balanced, Handicapped (you have advantage), and Privliged (AI Has advantage)
There is not alot of unit variety, but that is fine as you are on strategic level stuff, so you wouldnt see elite units and such.
My one complaint regarding units is actually with the one Unit you cannot recuit: Small Garrison. These start in your cities, at least with the 1914 campaign. In my opinion, they are too strong and should be alot easier for regular units to defeat, especially if they are isolated.
Also there should be ways to more easily destinguish between normal cities and fortress cities, as there were a few times where i took a city and an event popuped saying that city had been taken and that it was a great fotrress city.
Diplomacy is weak, the only action you can take against Neutral nations is declaring war. There should be some way of trying to convice neutral nations to join your side, especially since there is a bar showning the nation's view toward your side (sympathetic, neutral, resentful).
Beyond this i recommend reading the manual and watching Let's Play videos to get more of an idea, as i know i am going to miss stuff.
Bottom Line, i defienetly recommend Commander:The Great War, just be prepared to get sucked into long playsessions like i did, if you want a quick game, do the 1918 campaign.

Game Dev Tycoon mixed with the Sims 4. Might seem like an awesome combo, but really, it's very dissapointing.  All that you are going to do is pick up on tiny hints to make the game have no challenge while making videos. For the first few hours of gameplay I had no idea that, while making a video, it tells you what card genre you have to choose as the tutorial is nonexistent. Videos will take hours just to record as an hour in-game takes a very short while to surpass, editing will take around the same amount of time on longer videos too. It is much needed to slow down time while recording and editing, but speeding it up (or even having 1X 2X 4X etc time buttons) while idle.  In the early game (and I mean only for the first hour or two of gameplay) is the only time you'll be needing to work, as you only earn a small amount of money per published video. Otherwise, you can earn a ton more cash by just making videos all day every day, even after you've progressed to the better jobs. This makes the whole mechanic of working a flat line in progression. Another very annoying thing is that subscribers can barely go past a day without getting moody about no content from this one channel. What does this mean and why is it important? You can't practise skills that often, can't go out, can't socialize etc often enough since you will need to spend a large portion of the day just to keep your viewers happy.  This causes you to fall out with some friendly/romatical relationships easily, which makes the whole process of collaboration videos more difficult.
Meh. That just about describes it. It's just alright. Needs a lot of work in how realistic the viewers are. Videos are obsolete after a week, no binge watchers!? So what's my solution? For every passing week/month, the % of views will half depending on how many subs you currenty have. Such as this: Day 1 of video being published - views: 10K (100%). Week 2- views: 5K (50%). Week 3- views: 2.5K 25%. But videos will still never get low. How, you ask. You will still be gaining surbscribers with new videos, so then they will add to the "view %" of that week. Such as this: Subs: 10K. Views(W1) : 9k(100%). Subs: 20K. Views(W2): 10.8K(120%). Basically, how many more thousand subs you have, it will add 1% more on the old video views. How will this not Over Power famous YouTubers? The % will halve every week, keeping it around 70% during a good subscriber gain : "view %" deduction.

Cons:
Very, very meh gameplay

Ok. I have played this game for a while and got the hang of it.
It is a great game of WW1 with a couple of frustrating imperfections that you only really appreciate when you have played quite a bit. So while i might say negative things at the end of this review this is a recommendation.
For starters it feels like WW1.
The graphics look the part.  The map covers everything and there is plenty of open ocean for the naval campaigns to unfold.  The opening turns also develop in a  very similiar manner  to the actual war as long as you play even modestly sensibly as either side.
infantry battles are a hard slog.  A mistake in position can be very unforgiving.
Britain relies on convoys. The germans need to get their subs out or they will lose quickly.
The Austrians have no convoy resources to build gear or extra artillery shells but can maintain a respectable infantry force.
Battleship battles can be very important for morale.
All very WW1.
It has a great integration between the naval and land war, in that what happens in each is vital to your war effort, whatever side you are on.  It has a representation of all major theatres so you can decide to make your push where you want to. Want to quickly crush the Serbs? The Central Powers (germany,  Austria et al) must send all your artillery there first. But then it wont be in France or Russia for a couple of turns. Can you cope with that?
Although many reviewers have said artillery and other auxiliary units such as aircraft can be both over powered and under powered it really depends on the circumstances. Just a small amount can tip the balance. Even a shore bombardment might make all the difference to destroying a unit or letting it stay in place.. Having said that aircraft should really only be important for Recon in the first couple of years but even for recon they are a must have. Why have have Airships? They are fantastic for recon and  anti sub warfare.  As the Entente (Britain, France et al) i always build them to kill the German subs. Why have armoured cars? In open battlefields they can help cut vital supply lines and also have a recon role. They are a must have for the Turks on the Caucasian front.
Contrary to what many may think the tech tree and decisions there are vital.  German infantry start off better than every one else and it up to you to make it stay that way if you want to win as central powers.   There is a real infantry arms race that is apparent if you get to 1916 and havent done any upgrades of your infantry.  Also the tech tree allows both sides to get different nations to specialise. All nations should both do infantry and artillery trees but, for example, the brits can do naval and the French can do aircraft so you can sell your labs  you dont need and buy extra labs in the areas you like.
Ok whats wrong with this game?
Many reviewers have said the AI is over powered and cheats.
I think the AI is actually hopeless in the naval war and easily gets confused when battle lines open out as they do in Russia.
It does really silly early war builds such as many artillery pieces that can never be used because of shell shortages.
The AI as the central powers never builds enough subs to begin with and never really challenges the convoys that the british and french recieve. As an entente player you can use your subs in the Baltic,  armoured cruisers in the atlantic and light cruisers in norway and the Germans will be lucky to get 1 convoy through in the whole game. On the contrary when you play as the  central powers you can develop strategies to keep your convoys going or if necessary to restart them if they are stopped by entente naval warfare.
just on convoys the manual says you get an  10 manpower points per merchant ship that arrives. You actually get 100 and so if you get even ten convoys in that makes a 1000 which is more than most countries start with.  As the germans i start with around 1850 manpower points at the beginning of the war, by april 1916 in one game i had 2374 manpower points in germany. A great way to populate a country but not very realistic. As a note I have never actually played a game where man power made any difference to either side. Manpower quality is said to be in the game and occasionally you get a note saying its gone down but i have noticed the difference, however well or badly i was doing.
As Central powers you only build infantry,  subs and replacements for your 3 planes if they get destroyed..  Heaps of fluffy stuff can come later and will be useful (see later) but if you want to survive that is what you need.
As Entente the AI stuffs Egypt full of infantry, artillery and planes.  For gods sake it only needs 4 infantry 1 gun and a plane to hold there against what ever the turks can muster for years!  Also as the Entente it is pointless to try to conquer turkey from there. You do it by taking Constantinople from your position in  Serbia after crushing Bulgaria. The game system gives  the Entente 3 free infantry units in april 1915 offshore at gallipoli. never land at Gallipoli, send the Anzacs to Serbia where they will do a seriously good job.  The AI nearly always lands them at gallipoli where they get slaughtered.
The real fail in the AI of the  game though has been mentioned before by other reviewers and that is when italy joins the war most of the french and british units defending France all go to italy and capturing Paris becomes a walk in the park for the germans. Contrast this against the fact that in the many games i have played i have rarely won in france before italy joins the war so up to this point the game mechanics and balance has been extremely good in recreating a version of what actually played out in history. France was historically the battlefield where the horrible grind occurred and the war was won and lost in bitter battles on sea in the atlantic and in russia.
Lastly i will give you one of my secrets to winning as the germans if the game plays out past 1916.  Buy lots of artillery labs and build the railway guns. Dont bother with wasting money on buying much extra artillery shell production as the railway guns only use 2 artillery shells per shot rather than 10 for conventional guns. It also fires as well, if not better, than the normal guns, contrary to the manual. lastly its a railway gun so must stick to railways but Paris and every other main city or objective is on a railway.
Also to get your shell production up 5 shells a turn can easily cost 200 points . As the Central Powers do you want ten subs or ten infantry or 1 extra artillery shot every second turn.. thats a no brainer.

Just a couple of things for the AI to get right and this a all time classic strategy game, even against the AI. Obviously with an arranged game with another player none of these AI issues are a problem.
Still after all this 400 + hours tells me i love this game.  You will too.

World War I strategy games are few and far between as the conflict is mostly remembered for bloody stalemate in the West and the relative fluidity on the Eastern Front is largely unknown to the Western mainstream public. But World War I introduced the weapons and tactics that dominated the titanic struggle that was World War II.
Commander: The Great War is a "grand strategy" game that pits you as a leader of the Central Powers (Austro-Hungary, The German Reich, Turkey, Bulgaria) or the Entente Powers (Serbia, Belgium, France, Russia, United Kingdom, Italy, Romania) in the European, North African and Middle-Easternt theatre of operations. As such your main task is to defeat the opponents on the battlefield but you must also pay attention to your industrial otput, available manpower and research facilities. Gameplay is pretty straightforward and easy to master and even strategy novices should have no problem in being good at the game.
CTGW has a major problem in the field of AI as it tends to fall apart pretty quickly and pulls major offensives in secondary theatres while leaving their main frontlines critically exposed. I've managed to be victorious as Central Powers in 1916 by taking Paris in the West, Venice on the Italian Front and conquer Baltic provinces, Byelorussia and Kiev and Odessa in the East as AI concentrated its forces on the Apenine peninsula and Caucasus. Playing for Entente I was able to completely annihilate Central Powers in 1917 as Germany and Austro-Hungary kept sending reinforcements to the East leaving Western Front to collapse under the pressure of my armies. AI is also bad at utilising Entente preponderance in terms of warships as it gathers them in small flottillas instead of grand fleets making it easy for Central powers to defeat them in small engagements.
So playing CTGW against an AI is really not a challenge but thankfully there is PBEM options for those who would like to test their mettle against a human opponent. My frend and I have been playing for 4 days and in 1916 the war is still undecided and there have been epic offensives and counter-offensives on all fronts, fortresses and cities besieged and sieges lifted etc. This has been one of the best multiplayer strategy experiences in my gaming career.
So Commander: The Great War is somewhat a mixed bag. The basic premise is sound but it is let down by lackluster AI. Also, while there is a Diplomacy tab in game, it only contains overview of which country belongs to which alliance and players cannot spend any points in persuading countries to join their alliance. Also replayability factor is somewhat limited as AI always pulls the same historic maneouvres (Germans implement the Schlieffen plan in 1914, Russians launch offensives against East Prussia and Galicia, Allies land at Gallipoli in 1915 etc.) but multiplayer option lifts the game from the plains of mediocrity to the heights of a very good grand strategy. It still is no Hearts of Iron or Europa Universalis but it can stand proud on its own.

Ark Survival Evolved is a game that has recieved many positive reviews, and many negative ones, ever since its beta release in mid-2015. The game is now officially released but still contains many flaws, which many would say still outweigh the all the good stuff this game has to offer. In my personal opinion, I still greatly enjoy this game and there are reasons why.
In this review I'm not going to cover every single pro and con this game has to offer, as there a plenty of reviews on steam and on the internet that do that very well. I'm simply going to go over a few points I'd like to raise as well as warn players about.
Asside from it's very addictive nature, this game brings your childhood fantasies to life by throwing you into a massive pre-historic open world filled with 100+ species of different creatures you can tame. The story-line in this game is also something that seperates it from it's competitors in this genre of gaming, especially when you finish the game it reveals a considerable amount of backstory about the ARK and how you got there. Despite its flaws (which I'm not going to cover in this review) I would still find myself coming back to this game for thousands of hours of gameplay simply because I cannot get enough. I found that playing this game with friends only heightens that experience and makes it much more fun as you adventure and survive in this massive dinosaur world together. The game also offers 5 offical maps to play on (including it's latest expansion Aberration) as well as an extensive range of unnofficially made maps that are just as good. The two expansions, Scorched Earth and Aberration, offer more unique gameplay mechanics into the game as well as a unique and fantasic environment to survive in as well as a range of new creatures to tame. You don't need to purchase the expansions to really enjoy this game, but I would recommend them if you can afford it.
A few things I would like players to know before they want to get into this game:
1. This game is extremely time-consuming. You need to be prepared to spend hours and hours in building shelters, taming dinosaurs, and farming farming farming resources to advance through the game.
2. I would NOT recommend playing on official PVP servers as most of them contain an extremely hostile alpha tribe who wipe out anyone else on the server after a few days you joined, wasting all those hours you spent on your base and dinos.
3. Unnoffical servers are no where near as toxic and can be way more fun as they usually contain a friendly community you can play with.
4. Playing with friends makes this game MUCH more fun! :)
5. This game is extremely addicting so make sure you find time in your day to play!

Contrast is a beautiful game that I had picked up during the Steam Summer Sale. While there was some graphical glitches, the game was presented in a way that kept me playing. The scenery was stunning. The character models were okay. Cutscenes were a bit jittery, but it wasn't too bad.
Gameplay was good and responsive. It was kinda hard on the platforming, but that might be just me being bad at 3D platforming.
The puzzles presented in the game weren't too difficult, but weren't easy either. The 'shadow-shifting' was an interesting touch to puzzle mechanics. While the 'shadow shifting' was a bit buggy at areas, it didn't make the game 'not playable', you can still get through the game and enjoy it.
Though there were puzzles that I got stuck at, it felt wonderful solving on what to do.
And the story. Wow, I haven't really loved a story like this in a video game for quite a while. With the collectables in the game, the little snippets of newspapers and such, they enhanced the story even more. The music captivated me from the get go when I first even started up the game and I stayed captivated through out. The character development was choppy at times but each character was unique in their own personalities.
Contrast is a short game, but I enjoyed it. So if you like puzzles, platforming, and a story about helping a little girl and her family, then I recommend you to pick up Contrast.

TLDR: Interesting game with interesting ideas, smooth gameplay and a lovely story-presentation. Unfortunately too short and expensive (when not on sale) considering the amount of content it offers, but still worth a try.
Full review:
A short (REALLY short, finished it with 100% of the achievements in under 3 hours) platforming game which in a way reminds me of the Portal games since, as one of the game's achievements references to by name, rather than thinking with portals here you are "Thinking with Shadows". Can't reach your objective in the 3d perspective environment? time to start looking for a way to make the shadow of objects, buildings or "people" (even tho they are invisible to your eyes) help you, so that you can then shift into the walls and do 2d perspective platforming with the shadows. The fluidity in which you do this change between the 3d world and the 2d shadows is very smooth. Yes you will run into a few "buggy" spots but they are few and don't really break the gameplay.
Story-wise, it is a charm. You could consider it 2 stories, one of the young girl Didi's desire to be with her parents and to make them be happy, which is the focus point for most of the game's lenght, and a more subtle one which springs up near the end related to Dawn, the character you control, about who exactly is she and why she has the powers she has. Mind you, its not the best story ever but it works well for the game and the way it is presented is pretty good.
Again, short game and expensive considering the amount of playtime it can offer (I'd recommend buying it when it is on sale with a 60-ish or more % discount) but what little you get is in my opinion quality content worth checking out. Hopefully we see a similar premise, or maybe even a proper game sequel, in the future from this developer.

This game.. This game, man. If you're a fan of grand strategies and scifi, this is an excellent game for you. The obvious comparison is Stellaris, but there are plenty of differences; Endless Space has turn based actions, and is more focused on playing established, dev-crafted factions than making your own. But the fact that the factions and worlds are so heavily crafted by the devs very much comes out in its favour.
Endless Space has a rich, deep lore that really helps suck you in and help it stand out. The mechanics *are* excellent - I love the politics system that help make up your government and affect which laws you can pass, and the colonisation system and general empire-running system work very well. The "Manpower" system for running militaries is fantastic - I love the granularity, needing to make sure your military has enough willing recruits as well as strategic resources to build your ship, and the ground based combat is fun and engaging too. But honestly, the *lore* of Endless space is what keeps bringing me back - the universe the Endless left behind, and the Sci-fantasy theme of the planets and technologies you find on new worlds. Even the individual factions have plenty of personality, from the cyber-cult of the Vodoyani to the narcissitic single-person clone race of the Horatio. The world oozes personality and really drags me in.
The one thing I will say is that, like the rest of the Endless series, its not very good at explaining. Expect to restart a few games as you learn the mechanics and go "ohhh, i could do that all along? Dammit, this changes everything." Read a few guides or just learn by doing - the game has a tutorial, but its not the most transparent. But thats because it has so many granular mechanics, and once you learn them all you'll have a blast taking a new empire to the stars..

Okay, this game? It's bad. I mean, it's really bad.
The plot is the "always memorable" my village and family were attacked and now I have to avenge them kind of thing. Nothing spectacular here. The main character has the personality of a brick, and apparently three voices! Yeah, get this: on story cutscenes he'll sound like this tryhard British nobleman, with horrible voice acting that doesn't even match what the subtitles are showing. His second and third voices? Oh man.
He'll say the same canned 5 lines EVERY TIME he spots an object you can interact with, so get ready to hear "what this is, an object"; or the classic "haha, I'm going to get fat". I say he has two voices ingame because some of these definitely sound like Text to Speech, but when you're not moving, the third voice will come in and start singing...?
You'll traverse through 8 different levels, although if I were you I'd stop at the end of level 1. Level 1 allows you to hear this "amazing" voice acting by yourself, have a few laughs, and be in awe of how bad and glitchy this game is. It's like watching a bad movie with your friends, it has a few "so bad it's good" moments, high comedic value.
The gameplay..? Umm.. It's a spamfest. Yeah there's a skill list but I never paid attention to it, since most mobs just die by spamming the attack button. Even if they defend they'll eventually try to attack you but since you're already spamming you'll almost always attack first. The framerate gets godawful at times, and for this game, there's no reason. It looks like something out of PS2 games, and I have nothing against dated graphics, only poor optimization. I love how the game has ranged weapons, and you can use these, yet there is no normal enemy that thinks of even using a bow. Dark Souls this ain't.
There's this Survival Mode with leaderboards but the bad gameplay doesn't justify its presence whatsoever.
It also started putting in jumping puzzles in a certain level as if the engine itself is good for such things.
The soundtrack...? I remember it had tracks that looped for the entire level, and these can take a while. There's only one combat theme but I wasn't expecting variation there. No track comes to mind. Forgettable at best, annoying at worst.
I am fully aware this was a one man team development for this game and while that is admirable, doing such a sloppy job and making the game so glitchy (i've died randomly in midair, got launched to oblivion, got kicked around chasms, you get the point) and badly optimized won't give you an excuse to put this out there and expect praise. Especially when you're charging money for it.
Please don't waste your money on this.

This game is ever so much fun. Here's how it works:
Buy some ships and tell them where to go trade stuff.
Watch the money go up until you can afford more ships.
That's about it.
Everything else is basically a sandbox. You can fight pirates, for example, but you can either do that very early with an inadequate fleet that gets killed all the time... or sit around with your thumb up your butt until you have oodles of money and can afford big powerful ships the pirates can't kill. Or anything in between, really. But you're the one who decides when or if you fight pirates at all.
Similarly, you can buy a building permit in any town, and build a warehouse and residences and plantations and stuff, then run around dragging settlers to the town so they can live in the houses and work at the plantations and put stuff in the warehouse. Or you could, you know, NOT. Or, again, anything in between.
But if you combine this with telling your fleet where to trade stuff, you can make one city produce a whole bunch of bananas and another city produce a whole lot of cotton so your fleet can trade cotton and bananas back and forth between those cities and make oodles of money. Then you can combine this with fighting pirates and use the oodles of money to buy big powerful ships.
There's also some sort of diplomacy thing that goes on, but it's very shallow and pointless. If people don't like you, sell them stuff until they like you. By the time anyone is trying to fight with you, chances are you're filthy rich and sailing a fleet that can drop-kick them over the horizon. It's honestly difficult to make people dislike you, anyway. You essentially have to attack their ships and steal their stuff, but why would you do that when you can just sail your own fleet around and make oodles of money?
Oh and there's some kind of campaign or something that is basically a bad animation playing in a window while a bad voice actor tells you what to do. Then he sits around and waits for you to do it, unless of course you don't care, and then you'll be playing for hours before he pops up all suddenly because you accidentally did what he wanted.
There's no actual challenge here. It's very casual. If you like this sort of a thing, then this is the sort of a thing you will like. Also, I like the word "oodles." Oodles, oodles, oodles. It's almost as much fun to say as "quark."

Short review:
9+. Best WW1 TBS game out there at the moment. The hardcore strategy meter for this game is mediocre, so you don't have to be a Gary Grigsby fan to enjoy this one. Average game takes about 20 hours to finish.
Long review:
Commander: The Great War is a turn-based grand strategy game (warfare, production, tech research) with panzer general style combat, that plays out on one map of Europe (no different maps for tactical battles) . You can play either as Central powers or Entente. Once a nation joins your side, you control all their assets.
Troops consist of land troops (infantry, cavalry, armor, armored cars, artillery), air force (bomber&fighter), navy (subs, destroyers, battleships). Tech research is on those three fields (land,air,navy). Production is based on industry points received from cities (or trade ships if they reach harbour before sunk) and you can produce troops, rail network, ammunition production and naval transport capacity. You also get special generals to attach to your troops.
The game captures the trench warfare pretty well and especially on western front the lines tend to move slowly. The game is also pretty hard and I lost on the first try. The AI is pretty good and only on a few occasions I noticed stupid behaviour, like AI moving arty to the front lines. One big setback (IMO) is that the units gain no experience.

Not only can you charge into battle in a medieval age.. but i think this is the only game where you can charge into battle with nothing but your bare fists and start beating people to death while screaming for help. I rate it 10/10 giant midgets

I picked up this game because I am into time management simulator games, and was not dissapointed.  Especially for an early access game this is pretty nice.  I may have more detailed cons than pros, but don't take that as a turn off as this game IS still being developed.
Pros:
-Works well for those into time management simulators
-Nice Progression system with helpful nudges about what to do
-Exremely nice interaction with NPCs
-Early on this game can really hook you with the "story" as its cool and quirky
-Has a nice take for those who like collectables, as you can buy many items that are placed around your house to add a pleasing asthetic
Cons:
-The "Life" aspect of this game might go a bit too far with how hard it is to keep up with rent while staying friends with others, this wouldn't be an issue if it didn't come back to bite you in the♥♥♥♥♥  With the social aspect of this game being required, it seems more of a nuisance than anything.
-Many typos in English version
-In this game events happen where you can go to a location to talk to other YouTubers, get discounts on games and consols, or go to a convention.  These events are a very nice addition to this game, however, they are extremely frequent in tthe early game while LITTERALLY being non exsistant in late/end game.
-Game will sometimes delete previous actions when doing any of the following.
1. Creating a video
2. Going to an event
3. Exiting the game
-Not a game where you can pay attention to something else for a few minutes without somehow pausing.  Unlike most simulator games, wile you are choosing what to buy/card to pick/actions time continues to travel very fast, making it very difficult to keep up with the game without getting frustrated.
Conclusion:
As someone who has completed the game (at least what there is as of this review) I can say that these cons don't take too much away from the game until you get to late game.  Keeping in mind that this is still in early access, this game has VERY good potential, all the mechanics of this game compliment eachother nicely.  If you're just a casual gamer and want to laugh about the funny times that you'll have with this game, I HIGHLY reccomend this to you.  On the other hand if you are a hardcore gamer that likes to complete the challenges in games, I would not really reccomend this game to you.

I was watching for a long time for this wargame, cause I didnt fully understand what I'll get - Or this is just a Panzer Corps clone or something like AGEod wargames. I like both of 'em, but still had some questions, even that Slitherine(For me it's like a seal of quality) is game publisher.
Overall I'm really interested in any Great War staff(Books, Games, etc.), but there are only few good games in WW1 setting.
Finally I decided - It's time to try this title and I got interesting mixture between Panzer Corps and AGEod wargames.
Game offers few scenarios, each by starting year. You choose side by alliance - Entente or Central Powers, you can't choose and play only one country, but for WW1 wargames it's OK. But it wou,d be nice to see Entente devided by two more alliences(both on one side ofcource) - Western Entente and Russia with Serbia, cause these two theathers were historically "independent" even they fought on one side. But it's a feature which "would be nice to see".
In game you can produce units, research militsry staff(grenades, machineguns, gas, etc.), increace transport capacity by investing resources into railways, ship transport and etc.
Besides ground warfare, game offers naval and simplified aerial warfares(including strategic airship bombardment).
Graphics are eyecandy. In-game interface, town & officers photos, events along with sound effect and music deserve special attention - all of this provides you with nice experience.
By the way, game perfectly rins on touchscreen devices, which is really important for me(especially abibility to hover cursor above unit to calculate predicted losses, not all of wargames even if they work with touchscreens support this feature)
Overall game is looking and playing very nice. Despite it's looking simple it's hard to master game. I'm really happy that I finally decided to get this one. If you still questioning yourself, but intersted in Great War or looking for a good wargame - Get Commander: The Great War! :)
Очень долго присматривался к этой игре, т.к. не до конца понимал что получу в итоге.
То ли клон Panzer Corps, то ли что-то похоже на варгеймы AGEod, обе из перечисленных варгеймов мне очень нравятся, но терзали сомнения несмотря на то, что издатель Slitherine(что для меня является знаком качества).
Вообще тема Великой Войны меня всегда привлекала, но качественных игр, в любом жанре, по этой тематике можно пересчитать по пальцам.
Наконец-то я решился и взял Commander: The Great War. В итоге я получил гибрид Panzer Corps и варгеймов от AGEod.
Варгейм предлагает на выбор несколько сценариев разделенных по годам. На выбор 2 стороны - Антанта и Центральные Державы. Выбрать одну страну и играть только за нее невозможно - только союзы, что для Варгеймов по 1-й Мировой Войне помоему - плюс, единственное можно было-бы разделить Антанту на 2 части - "Западная Антанта" и Россия с Сербией, т.к. это 2 ТВД, которые на протяжении войны несмотря на нахождения стран в единном союзе были практически независимы друг от друга, но это скорее мое пожелание, чем недовольство.
Игра дает возможность производить боевые единицы, проводить исследования военной направленности, увеличивать транспортные возможности -инвестируя в Ж/Д линии, транспортные корабли и т.д.
Помимо наземных сражений игра предлагает морские и упрощенные воздушные операции(Включая стратегические бомбардировки с помощью дирежаблей).
Графика приятна глазу - аккуратно нарисованнные гекс, красивые эффекты и просто приятные модельки юнитов.
Игровой интерфейс, фотографии городов, офицеров и фото эвентов вместе с замечательным звуком и музыкой заслуживают отдельного внимания - все это вместе погружаетв игру очень сильно.
Так же игра отлично работает на тачскрин девайсах, что для меня сейчас очень важно(особенно функция при наведении курсора на юнита для прогнозирования результатов сражения, к сожалению не везде это есть)
В общем и целом игра очень приятная и несмотря на кажущуюся простоту довольно занятна. В общем я рад, что решился ее приобрести, если у вас еще есть сомнения, но вам интересна тема Великой Войны или вы ищете занятный варгейм - смело берите "Commander: The Great War"! :)

Where I feel this fame falls a little flat is combat. It's a rather simplistic system, that feels more like it was ported from a smartphone app, than built for a PC release. And attacking towns is even worse, giving you absolutely NO control oncce your trrops have landed. In addition the fact that there is inly one possible map greatly reduces replay value in my opinion. Given what I know about the previous games in the series, while having upgraded graphics, seems to have downgraded gameplay in exchange.
That said, do I still reccomend it? Absolutely YES. You will certainly get your monies worth out of it, and I can see it being one of those games you pick back up every few months to take further advance your conquest of the Carribean.

Please ignore the time put into this game.  There are massive grinds for achievements in this game...
is a very frustrating runner game created in Unity...and it's the 2nd runner I've played involving a dog (the first being
, who is playable in this game as well.)  As like with many runners, you die...often.  The music will be burned into the depths of your mind as you grow increasingly frustrated from constant failures.
If you get enough letter pickups, you unlock ONE CHANCE at a minigame to play.  Learn it fast, because if you don't, you're dead.  If you want to replay the same event, you must get all the letter pickups two more times.   Why 2 more times?  Because the game is set to put the two minigames in rotation.  If you've beaten one and only want to play the other, you must trigger the minigame you want by only reaching the minigame you don't want to play.  If that's not bad enough, you often get repeat letters you don't want.  Example:  "U, U, U, X, U, U, P, U, U, U, U, G, U, U, X, U, O, X, P, U, U"  (That's recorded from a single run of actual gameplay)
There appears to be a visual error where "coin" pickups (which unlock character skins, a few with a different playstyle) can either be picked up twice by being touched once, or they simply don't appear (the latter is true of chests, which grant 5 "coins").  You'll find coins to be absolutely worthless when you unlock the last character.  There's also a questionable hitbox when it comes to certain areas and certain characters (much like the final character you unlock).
But not everything in
is bad.  The game's visuals are pretty good and the programming for the section randomizer is pretty well-done (though some areas will get repetitive and you'll find areas that are devoid of letter pickups...some balancing is in order).
Is it worth your money?  Although it looks good, my experience leads to a disappointing "no".  For the same money, you'll be better off with
(which has schoolgirls and pantsu).  I can't stop you from making your purchase, but if you value your sanity and don't enjoy a stressful experience of frustration and hair-tearing frustration...you might want to think twice.  It's not a BAD game...I just don't recommend it due to the stress it induced.

I first got Halo Wars for the Xbox 360 as a gift from a friend. We played it over and over again, for good reason too. The game has spectacular controls for a console RTS game. The visuals were stunning and still are on the Xbox. There are plenty of maps, each with good design, allowing for flanking and surprise attacks, letting no game become dull. Every faction has its unique abilities and when used correctly in collaboration with others, can be used very strategically.
So naturally, when this game was ported to PC, I was quite curious. I kept my eye on it for a little while until, not long after its release on Steam, the same friend who bought it for me on the Xbox bought it on Steam, for me, and himself.
Let's start off with the positives of this game: it is indeed the same game, with all of the greatness of the Xbox version, the visuals have been improved,—not to the extent people like to boast, but still, improved,—it is the definitive edition of the game, which means you will get access to all of the DLC released for the game over its lifetime on Xbox and lastly, the campaign has hours upon hours of play-ability; when you eventually get board of it, the skirmish mode has intelligent AI and offers unique games every time.
Now for the things I don't like: the controls on mouse and keyboard are not nearly as good as a controller, which is a great shame; they feel clunky and unresponsive; don't get me wrong, the game can still definitely be played with a mouse and keyboard, but I feel that using the controller is still a better option. The multiplayer is absolutely dead, period. The controls cannot be rebound, at all, for whatever reason. (Using "Insert" and "Delete" to rotate is a nightmare,) and finally, it is a console RTS, which means it isn't nearly as comprehensive as something like StarCraft II.
All-in-all Halo Wars: Definitive Edition is an excellent remaster of a great game, in which you can spend untraceable hours surviving the Covenant, or exterminating the human race. It provides a great mix of other timeless RTS games' formulas, such as StarCraft II and Age of Empires II, but also, from what I think it took the most inspiration, Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds, for its use of the Rock, Paper Scissors mechanic.
Halo Wars is definitely worth looking into; prepare to experience battles of epic proportions...

Nothing is more satisfying than inheriting a large kingdom through a multi-generational plan involving series of assassinations, while simultaneously fighting off your religious enemies and enacting your masterfully designed eugenics program (to produce the perfect heir).

The reason this gets a negative review is because the puzzle mechanic, art direction and voice acting are all superb with a lot of promise but ultimately falls short mostly because the game itself is very short. Disappointment is the main culprit that robbed this beautiful game of a glowing review.
If you manage to beat the game (don't worry it will only take you a couple of hours) you'll notice that the credits list a lot of talent that seems to never make an appearance in the game. For example, they credit contortionists and fire breathers, but I never saw any of those in the game. This gives me the impression like many others that this was originally meant to be a much more ambitious project but either time or budget constraints crippled the final product.
The plot also seemed a little hodgepodged if you asked me. There seemed to be a lot of useless plot tidbits and the parts that needed a lot more fleshing out were not.

Another beautiful indie game!  Last year it was Jamestown for me, this year it might well be Dustforce.
This is a great looking, acrobatic/ninja-rific platformer with a chilled out electronic score and a nice scaling difficultly level.  Imagine Meatboy, but way less frustrating and soul-crushingly difficult, plus more move variety, and rewarding combat. (!)
While levels can be beat without necessarily being an ace player, for me there's a strong, strong "I know I can do better" urge after completing a run, so there's a lot of value here if you're a perfectionist.  And the game's beautiful graphics, balletic animations and excellent level design always reward me for coming back to previous challenges.
Lastly, the ability to watch replays of the top players is also an excellent addition, both to help you see how others solved tricky spots and to help you improve your game.
This is a real gem, grab it if you like platformers with style!
EDIT: I've enjoyed my time with Dust Force, but unforunately I feel like I've hit the skill ceiling.  I've gotten to a point in the levels where I'm just not good enough to progress further, and don't think it's worth my entertainment time to put in the hours to get better.  This in NO WAY is the fault of the game or it's developers.  I still think Dust Force is amazing, but unfortunately I just won't be able to crack open its higher level content.

We should adress the good first, because what's good about this game is really good. The setting and tone of 1920's noir is brilliant and it shines through in every area; it feels like a mixture between the Sierra Madre and Bioshock's Rapture with the unique lighting, it is one of the best looking worlds ever seen in a game. Additionally, the voice acting is pretty solid and its interesting how you never see the side character, but you see their over the top body language in their shadows, which is quite entertaining in a Vaudville/Groucho Marx way. On top of all of this, the story is pretty good and surprisingly charming.
However, that's really the end of the good stuff. Like Limbo, contrast has a really good idea, but fails to do anything interesting with it past the very first puzzle.
Almost every puzzle is a varitaion of pressing a button to make something in the room move, which creates a shadow ramp.
Unfortunatley, there are two big problems with the shadow platforming, which is supposed to be the star of the show.
The first problem is that you will periodically stop being a shadow. You'll be standing somewhere and if you hit something (because shadows act like solid objects) you might instantly get out of shadow mode.
The second problem is that the platforming is pretty shotty with landing detection and there are times where it looks like you should be able to make it, only to clip through the shadow, meaning you have to start all over. This is especially problematic during the second act, where you have to climb a massive building using the shadows of a carrosel to climb a large rotunda. If the platform detection messes up at all, you have to start all over.
Additionally, there's an entire section of this game that is a direct "homage" to Limbo. A section in which you run away in a dark shadowy world from a giant spider. This amounts to about 1/10 of the whole experience, which really shows that the developers were running out of ideas at this time.
Because of its incredible short length of about 3-4 hours, its boring and repetative puzzles, and its buggy gameplay I can't reccomend this as a game, but I can recommend it for its story and style

The tunnels are claustrophobic, the make you feel constricted you hear a noise at the other end you have no choice but you go find it and throw a knife at it. and those ♥♥♥♥ing bugs that you have to scare away with your light, pure nightmares. The surface is equally a scary, even scarier at some points, from little fish that spit green snot at you, to huge flying beasts that are sooooo hard to kill, and are even harder to get away from if you're out in the open. The surface is a marvel to look at, and had me stop and looking around for stuff. Running out of filters is a ♥♥♥♥ING nightmare on Ranger, run out of those and you are dead unless you can find some lying around.
Cons: Agh, this game is not easy, this is not a con for some people, but sometimes I just like going balls deep and firing all my weapons into the faces of my enemies, but this game is like ♥♥♥♥ that. Walk around with a silenced EVERYTHING and spam throwing knifes, which at some times can be frustrating and difficult but not impossible. At some times the enemy AI can be completely brain dead at, other times they can hear you squeeze one out 20ft away from them. I did experiecne that bug that stopped me from finishing the game without wiping my save completely, so I have yet to finish Metro: Last Light, this is a HUGE problem and completely broke the immersion for me, and forced me to stop playing, on the other hand the time I did play was fantastic and a absolute treat. But this needs to be fixed ASAP, very big problem, and it seems to be quite popular simple search on the Internets proved that for me.

The concept behind Dustforce is really pretty cool. It's basically Super Meat Boy with some sort of janitors as main characters. You defeat enemies by slamming them with your broom while running/jumping/gliding/sliding around the level (Meat Boy style !) sweeping the leaves that lay around. You get scored for speed and effectiveness and it's actually extremely difficult. Especially if you want to earn S ranks for every level.
The thing is... the controls just don't feel right. Controllers aren't automatically recognized and configured so you have to do that yourself. A controller definitely works better than a keyboard, I can tell you that, but if you don't know how to properly set it up it's still really hard to play.
I did finish Super Meat Boy, but I won't be able to finish this until they succesfully implement controller functionality without the player having to mess around with it.
Controller issues aside, this is a great game that just needs to be experienced.

This is an excellent sidescrolling single-player or co-op shmup. I have only played solo so far. I imagine with 4 people playing the action is quite hectic. You select a mech and have several loadout choices for each mission. Missions are done in three stages, at the completion of each stage you are awarded a choice between 3 upgrades that improve attack power, defense, shield regeneration or the speed you acquire special attacks. At the completion of a mission you can spend your mission bonus to buy more upgrades from a vendor.
Controls are very tight and the game is well-balanced, not over-the-top difficulty like some of the borderline sado-masochistic shmups you can find on Steam.
Overall lots of fun and worth considering in a genre that is filled with good options.

Pros:
* Mechs have well defined roles (tank, ranged dps, melee dps, and evasion) which allows for synergy between players (tanks deflecting bullets and making everyone invincible to help those who are less familiar with this type of arcade-style game, sniper marking targets to take more damage from all sources, melee dps slowing time for everyone, ...)
* Good amount of customization between picking a mech, a main weapon, and a sub weapon, which are all available immediately. Also frequent upgrades (usually 2) in the middle of levels that allow you to build towards your defined style (such as being a sniper and picking up crit upgrades) as well as a shop at the end of each level that allows for spending points towards more upgrades.
* Tons of game customization (enemy durability, player shot speed, hibox radiuses, spawn rate, fire rate... just about all low level manipulation you can think of). Lots of presets available, so you can easily switch between 5 difficulties' worth of settings, as well as extra presets like "Iron Man" where you have 0% shield multiplier.
* Lots of environments - from frozen skies to exploding suns, underwater wrecks to alien hives, gas giants to robot factories, there's 10 locations in all with quite a bit of variety.
* Can jump right in with the gauntlet mode - basically a never-ending mode (well, until you die) where you go for the high score.
Cons:
* Story dialogue / plot is seemingly intentionally bad, but just ends up being unfunny and adding very little. Anime avatars for the characters seem a bit out of place. Wish I could turn it off entirely.
* Would really benefit from having online multiplayer (as well as would probably sell a ton more copies. I know I'd be able to get some more friends to play it with me if it had online).
* Achievements would be a nice touch, as it would give me more reason to play and try out all the mechs / weapons solo (and more reason to spend time in gauntlet mode).
Other:
* Pretty quick game - around 2-3 hours. Want to call this a con, but can be a pro if you have trouble spending lots of time with friends after school/work since this game only has local co-op - it does mean you can beat this game in one sitting though, from start to finish.
* Music is ok (opinion), although if I bought the soundtrack it'd probably only be for a few tracks (namely the last boss ones, because that fight had multiple phases and is pretty exciting)
Update Feb 2016 - it does look like they are listening to users, and they added a bunch of new upgrades, a new level, steam achievements and a bunch of other little features while I wasn't looking. Definitely a plus, and it rips out one of my few cons about the game.

I am somewhat torn on this game. Being a long time grand strategy gamer and somewhat of a fanatic of the genre, I am torn between rating this game coming from that perspective and from the perspective of someone else.
For a die-hard strategy gamer this game probably won't satisfy your desire for WW1 combat on the PC. I will however recommend you purchase the Ipad/whatever version if you have one of those devices, as I can see it easily being a favorite to play when you are on the go. I would also recommend it to the die-hard people for online matches when you want to squeeze a match into a busy or exhausting schedule but don't have the time to get invested in something deeper.
For the average strategy gamers I easily recommend this game. It does a fairly good job at modelling WW1 warfare, though it is still a little too fluid on the Western front and advances are too easy in the East. There are a number of interesting tactical choices to make, though strategically you won't find yourself doing much different from what happened historically. The graphics are nothing too impressive, but there are some nice bits of flavor like how the unit cards display each nation's unique uniforms and the changes they experience as you progress in tech (picklehaubes to stalhelms for instance). I can also see  newer strategy game players getting a lot out of multiplayer.
So to sum it up, if you are a die-hard strategy gamer get this on a mobile platform and look for something else on PC, but if you are new to strategy games or maybe totally unfamiliar with First World War tactics, events, history, you should have a blast.

It offers some combination-based combat, but I don't find myself really using it, and the controls are a little wonky and would benefit from less vertical clamping, which feels very limited at times. I would also much rather see a standard shift key run option than the current double tap [W] key. Overall, it's a pretty simple hack and slash wih tons of cool artwork, that kept me entertained for hours. It should also be noted that it's a wildly impressive showing of what a single developer can do with the Blender Game Engine.

I should start out by saying that I am indeed somewhat biased. I've been following this game since I was in community college several years ago. I found the game because it was a WIP being created in the Blender Game Engine - something I was learning to use at the time. The developer's accomplishments even then absolutely astounded me, and I became dedicated to following his every update.
Reading some of the negative reviews, I feel like people are expecting this game to be something that it isn't. This game was never going to have the quality of a game created by a team of vastly experienced developers. This was created by one man using his own knowledge and experience to work with a rather complex and somewhat limited open source engine to create a game.
In my opinion, this game will best be enjoyed by those that are interested in using open source tools like Blender to create a video game. It shows what's possible - what you can do. There aren't a lot of projects out there like it, and those projects that do exist are rarely completed by their developers (one game, Elpis, is another that I followed around the same time that I started following Krum. It looked great at the time, but development eventually died off). Seeing the developer of Krum never give up despite the challenges he faced in development was encouraging and inspiring.
Seeing Krum appear in the Steam Library at last - and receiving the email with my CD-Key - was like a dream come true. Years and years of watching development, stalking a YouTube channel, and hoping that I wouldn't see the update stating that he'd cancelled the project had finally paid off. I downloaded the game and started playing, and I've not been disappointed. The game is excellently created considering it was completed by one man using an open source game engine. Not only that, but the game is still being developed and updated!
So, in conclusion:
If you set your expectations in the right place, you won't be disappointed by this game. Expect this game to be what it is: a personal project created by one developer with limited experience, using all of his own assets and skills to create something with an open source game engine. Don't expect a project that will be on-par with the Game of the Year created by a large team of developers. This game is excellent for what it is, and I'm proud to have followed it all these years.

This and the original Bioshock Remastered are both heartbreakers.
Just looking at the quality of the games, they are two of the finest FPS games ever made.  Though the second has a very weak first half of the game, it finishes strong.  Both games are must play titles, in my opinion, with the first being a serious contender for greatest FPS of all time.
Unfortunately, we are also looking at the quality of the port.
The port is awful.  There are sound bugs, control bugs, graphics bugs, and crashing bugs.  I crashed well over 50 times on each title, and that is not an exaggeration.
I thought that the games were so incredible that I still enjoyed them in spite of all the problems, and I slogged through them even when my experience was little more than "load save, take a step, crash, load save again."  Even though I was able to enjoy them, I do not think this is an experience I would recommend to others.  If you are going in, be aware that you may have massive issues.  Since I have played, they have released a patch that hopefully fixes some of them.  If you are not able or willing to play this on consoles, then be aware that you may have to constantly troubleshoot this game.  If you can get through it, the game itself is wonderful.

Community.
When I first looked at the server list I didn't know whether to burst out in laughter or continue staring. There are WAY too ♥♥♥♥ing many dedicaded servers with almost absolutely nobody on them...At all... I don't know if people are hanging out staring at the server list waiting or what the deal is.
I say that because I joined a game with about two players already on it, then after a couple rounds the server out of nowhere exploded with players. No bots and no joke. So yea, chances are people are waiting until they see a server with more than three users on it.
If you're into sci-fi shooters or are no stranger to half-life then ye, feel free to check this out. If you're a Gmod user then I don't see why you wouldn't download it- even if it's for the sake of props, and if you like run n' guns like Quake- oh what the hell, I'm no professional reviewer. Deeply disappointing, for MANY reasons.
The story of this game is excellent... the artwork and visuals are stunning, the gameplay is fun and engrossing, and so on and so on.
And a "remastered" version of a game (with all the original's positives and yet with fixes and improvements) sure sounds awesome.
But... that's not this game.  Because, while the original program is really good,  and so forth... the folks you put this into the "final shipping configuration" seem to have wanted to push folks onto the consoles and away from the PC.
Why do I say this?
Simply because there are "show-stopper" issues in the game which could not POSSIBLY have been "accidentally missed" during development, and which have still, to date, not been fixed.
In my own case, the "show stopper" is the infamous "no sound" bug.  Evidently, they wrote the "update" using a development kit focused purely on a specific console, and then "sorta-ported" it to PC, but never bothered to test it?   Basically, my game runs fine, and looks OK, but I get no sound except for in the full-motion-video pre-recorded sequences.
I've heard that people have been able to fix this, in some cases, by totally reconfiguring their PC's sound system.  NOPE.  Not gonna happen.  My PC's sound system is perfectly fine, and works with pretty much everything else out there.  The defect isn't with my PC, or with my PC's hardware, or with my PC's settings.  It's with a program which simply will not run properly on anything but the "target hardware" (that is, on the CONSOLE IT WAS DESIGNED TO RUN ON.)  Having to change sampling rates, or speaker configurations, or plugging and unplugging microphones, or the like, is NONSENSE.
There are many other issues as well, but I haven't PERSONALLY experienced any of them yet (because it's not worth playing a game without any sound!)
The original PC release still works just fine, by the way.

In my honest opinion, only hardcore Ark fanboys can recommend this game.
PRO-I enjoy this game, I play single player and it's a fun little sandbox with dinosaurs.
PRO-It's a fairly engaging experience and you may have fun building up if you can ignore or get around CONs 1-3.
CON-1. Holy #$%^ this game is a huge waste of time, literally.  Takes a long time to get anywhere.  Requires hauling lots of resources back and forth to build a base.  Taming one creature and take days just for the actual process, not including gathering the resources for it.  This seems to be preferred by some people that think wasting time makes the achievement more meaningful.  Not much of a problem if you jack up rates on a private server, so not a problem for me.
CON-2. The building system is ridiciously bad.  Hard to make structures even look even and hard to make contraptions that work due to restrictions designed for pvp; but you can somewhat alleivate this by installing CON-3
CON-3.  You have to download a #$%^load of mods to improve on all the flaws in the game.  Or at least a couple if you don't want to experience extreme frustration with the building system, among other things.
CON-YOU-SHOULDN'T-GET-THIS-GAME-FOR-PC.  Really the only reason I would NOT recommend this game, and it doesn't even have anything to do with gameplay.  People that claim requirements for this game are not high are full of #$%^.  Every major update requires 100+ GB of free HD space to install.  Seriously, you're expected to keep how many movies worth of space open just to play ONE GAME?  A lot of people had to uninstall more than a couple of games to update this ONE GAME.  And of course you can't play it online of Steam unless you update it, so, there you go.
Enjoy wasting 100 GB of HD space or headaches everytime a major update comes along.  This is why I believe only major fanboys could defend this game, since they don't even consider the above a thing; and I could understand that if you only play Ark all day.  I don't have a potato PC, I have other games I want to play.
Update:  They also regularly update the game with 100 MB ~ 2GB patches; and I found out that a portion of the community endorses this, because they like their "hotfixes".  So, if you like regular updates vs. their biweekly 20 GB updates on console, I guess this game is for you.

This is one of those instances where the review system needs a "neutral" option.  I can't really say this game is "Recommended" or not.  Instead, I'll provide one or two angles to consider if you are pondering a purchase (hey, it aint that expensive so...)
If you are taking this game out of some nostalgic feeling induced by hours and hours of PR 1 or PR 2 gameplay - get ready for a cactus in the rear end.  You'll love it for the first four, maybe five hours but then the dissapointment will set in.
Why?
Well, each of us who have had the pleasure of playing PR2 (and lets face it, those of us who really love games like PR2 are well underserved in the current market) will have had specific attributes of that game that we loved.   The obvious candidates there are:  Building up your very own trade enterprise, building up a fleet through combat or cash (face it - taking em is better and you get better ships too), getting your own island and MAKING it the way you like it (i.m.o the best part about the game).  Then there's the cheesy sword fights which I personally got bored of quite quickly, the ship combat which was rather well done even though it can get a bit monotonous after a while and so on.  Right?  Well remove about half of that and you have Port Royal 3.
You can't win a patch of land anymore to build your own town and see it grow.  The trading dynamic, although majorly the same as PR2, just feels horribly less than what PR2 had to offer.  The supply and demand system from PR2 had been greatly lessened (or dumbed down?) and seems to be less dynamic in PR3.   Ship battles, although still barable in PR3, is a far cry from the enjoyable model we had in the previous title.
What would you have expected in a new Port Royal title?
Well - for one, everything that made PR2 awesome plus the multiplayer that just about 99% of all loyal Port Royal 2 players CRIED for (and we cried...).  Sure enough we have multiplayer, but dear god what a lazy attempt at a multiplayer experience this has been.   Fair enough - a title such as this where gameplay isn't measured in one or two hours, but days or even weeks, mplay is a very challenging thing.  Out of the seven or so possible routes to go for such an experience, they opted to go for the tecnically simplest and quickest to implement.  That's just cheap.
One would also have expected that the AI and the dynamics of the supply and demand system be tethered to some kind of tangible link that leads all the way to colonists within towns.  Though this is in SOME measure true, it falls horribly short and this is where a massive failure from the studio rears its ugly head.  This is a game that attracts those of us who like to tweak, fiddle and tinker, crunch the numbers and see the results in terms of profit and the likes.  You took that away from us in some attempt to make the game (i guess?) accessible to a different crowd [is that the case? stop making games please]
It is almost as if this game is trying to build on the marginal success of Port Royal 2, yet trying to aim at a different crowd..but not quite sure which one.   I might obviously be very wrong here.  Either that or games like this, which require some mental fortitude (i mean the previous title), has become dumbed down (by design or perhaps by the quality of those at the helm of the development) over the years.
So this all seems horrible - it is, only if you come from the Port Royal 2 camp.
If you are NOT familiar with the previous titles and a mangement style game is your thing then THIS is the game you start with before you move UP in the ladder to play port royal 2 (no mplay in pr 2 unfortunately).
For you new guys to the title:
It's a quaint and simple introduction into management style games based on the colonisation boom during the 1600's (more or less?) in the carribean.  yarr pirates and all of that.  You'll figure out quite easily how to set up trade routes, make a buck and play with the very simple concept of buy low sell high vs volume and demand manipulation.  Unfortunately the latter is not as much possible as in the previous entry of this title.  Look at this as a colourin book of sorts which will prepare you for the more mentally satisfying experience of games like PR2, the guild, patrician and so on.
It's a great gift for your 12 year old or if you have a friend who recently suffered a severe head injury and is struggling to add apples - this is the game you'll use.
Personally [THIS IS AIMED AT YOU, DEVS] I do hope that a new entry in this title comes - Port Royal  4.  I hope the devs take the experience gained from the franchise thusfar and build a superior product.  [granted also, the company has changed hands and changes obviously affect such things - not to be too hard on pr3].
Here's to hoping (the gaming industry...god help us..)

If you are expecting a GTA style world, turn away. It's a fairly simple map designed to provide some simple entertainment for getting you from point A to B, and to give some room for foot and car chases that are not at all as intense as they are in the GTA games. The shooting moments are so simple and short that they seem completely unnecessary.
The main mechanic of the game is both it's strongest and weakest point. The itoregation process is innovative and interesting. At the same time it often leaves you feeling out of control. As your character often phrases things horribly and not at all as you expected, leaving you to deal with the outcome. In a way you don't just have to figure out what the suspect is thinking, but you have to figure out what your own character is thinking too.
It can be tedious, for example (no spoilers): In the middle of the game you investigate several murders, one after another. From the very beginning your character suspects they are all committed by the same person. The victims all have a similar profile and died under similar circumstances. Which means you play through multiple scenarios that are very alike, it gets boring. Despite his suspicions you go through the motions of investigating and arresting other men, even though both your character and you suspect that these men are innocent. The game forces you to do it though, making it feel very guided and that your choices make no difference.

Upsides to this game:
-The music is gorgeous. The Streets, House on Fire, and Kat's Song are my favourite tracks from the soundtrack.
-The concept is brilliant. Shifting between 3D and 2D? Love it.
-The atmosphere is stunning. You are all alone in your world, invisible, but you see Didi's story going on around you. Did I mention the music?
-Exploration is rewarded. Little bits of backstory, easter eggs here and there, but invisible walls ruin that a tad.
-The story is a simple, small story involving a young girl and her family. No threat of world domination, extinction, etc. Just a little girl who wants her family to be together. It's very touching, and all the more powerful because you can only watch from the sidelines, seeing their silhouettes act out the drama.
Downsides to this game:
-The puzzles can require spot-on timing and aiming.
-The camera and controls can feel awkward.
-It's very short. I played through it twice to 100% in just a few hours. A little pricey for the length, but if it's on sale, grab it (the soundtrack too)
-Didi can be a little annoying at times.
TL;DR (you lazy bugger you):
Short with a few annoyances, but the atmosphere and story are amazing, and far outweigh the bad. Get it and the soundtrack when it's on sale.

After reading other reviews, I am strongly convinced most of negative opinions are based on poor understanding of this game's mechanics. Also reviewers mentioning balance problems mostly posted before the recent 1.6 patch which I base my experience on.
CTGW is a nice addicting hex-strategy title, which provides a depth approximately compared to the Panzer Corps series (being totally different though). It is not too heavy to chew to keep you occupied a whole evening to do one turn. Still it isn't too light to bore you. The shallow approach (compared to grand strategy titles of a Gary Grigsby level) turns out to open up the chance of plenty of quick fun. The well known one-more-turn-desire might catch hold of you very soon.
People complaining about not succeeding in any kind of Blitzkrieg advances should remember this game is all about WW1. This means trench warfare and the chance to see frozen fronts for long durations of time. It is possible to break through after all, but this requires some patience and the application of accurate forces.
Overall after the 1.6 patch I perceive the devs did a very good job in balancing forces. AI may have some flaws but like any other strategy title you will find the real challenge in a play against another human only.
MP is handled via external servers very similar to PBEM. It is Igougo sending your turn to the slitherine server. The server then informs your opponent by mail. The Opponent then logs into the game which loads down your turn, and so on.
Considering the mid segment pricing I can without hesitation recommend to get this, if you generally like strategy titles and also share the interest to lay hands on the remarkably underrepresented WW1-theme.

Commander the great war is an exceptional world war 1 tile based strategy game with an extraordinary amount of depth and replayability. After reading other negative reviews this game has recieved i was struck by how ridiculous they were. Well over half of them state that the ai cheats. That the ai has huge production bonuses and can produce three times as many units as human players. That the ai's units recieve combat bonuses that make them twice as strong as the human players units. All these claims are simply not true. However i can understand how many players have come to these false conclusions.
- The ai are very good for a turn based strategy game and may provide a serious challenge to newcomers.
- The strategy's you must use to triumph are so vastly different to all other strategy games, simply because the first world war was and still is so vastly different to any other wars that have ever been fought.
- The attacking unit will always take far more damage than the defending unit (up to four times in fact!!!) therefore to overwhelm a single enemy infantry unit is not uncommon to have to attack it with 3 of your own infantry units and only after you have weakened said enemy infantry unit with artillery bombardments and harried them with fighters.
Many players have also claimed that artillery, fighters, armoured cars, bombers, zeppelins and cavalry are useless and unbalanced. While there may have been some serious balance issues in 1.5 the recent release of the 1.6 beta patch has fixed 90 percent of these balance issues. As for these units being useless even prior to the patch this was never the case. Artillery may appear to do little damage but the small amounts of damage they do in addition to the damages in efficency they cause to enemy units are invaluable and are almost required to make any kind of serious pushes into enemy territory. Fighters and bombers function as aerial artillery and there large range and high sight values make them very usefull as scouting units. Zeppelins have the highest range and sight and this more then makes up for there lack of durability and the drain they will inflict on your precious ammo stockpiles. Armoured cars are twice as fast as infantry units can see four time as far. This makes them usefull scouting units. What cavalry lack in defense they make up for in speed, sight and offensive capabilitys.
Commander the great wars singleplayer will eventually get dull. However the multiplayer never will i hope you have enjoyed my rambling review and that you will like it to prevent any firther loss in sales this game may suffer due to false accusations of cheating ai.

KRUM - Edge Of Darkness
Hack'n'slash RPG
HA Studio ltd.
HA Studio ltd.
in an Hack'n'slash RPG developed and published by HA Studio ltd., a 1-man studio.
The game's story is your run-of-the-mill fantasy story, only without anything interesting: an army of orcs, undead and other creatures destroys everything in their path, and you play as a farmer hellbent on getting revenge for the murder of his father, family and uncle.
The game does look pretty good for a 1-man job. However, there are a lot of bugs and glitches that I found while playing the game: ragdolls getting stuck in the floor or ceiling, missing ground in which you fall to your death, no skybox at the bottom of pits... Also, most of the enemies that you face all look and fight the same, adding to the overall biggest flaw of the game: its repetitiveness.
The game tries to be like one of those old-school action games that I grew up with (Rune, Gothic and Drakan being a few examples), and at the beginning I was having a blast. But after 30 minutes, and having killed the 8th enemy in the game, I understood what I got into. The game suffers from repetitiveness: while you do have combos for your weapons, most of the time you will just keep mashing the attack button to kill your enemies. You also have long-ranged weapons, but they are really useless and deal much less damage than axes or swords.
Every enemy drops some items and its weapon, giving you the possibility to change your weapons (that keep degrading). Unfortunately, they all feel the same, making the use of one over the other pointless. Exploring the environments also feels lifeless, and choosing to go straight to your objective rather than engaging in fights feels more satisfying than it should be.
The only challenge lies in the combat. You will encounter two types of AI: one first parries, then attacks, then parries, then attacks... and the other just keeps attacking till it runs out of stamina. Both of those can be easily defeated if you understand who you are fighting. Otherwise, once you get hit by the latter AI, you are doomed to die since just a couple of hits will kill you, especially in the beginning of the game. Most of the time I found myself more frustrated than challenged, and that's not all that fun.
The voice acting is just as cheesy as I wanted it to be. However, the voice of our hero often feels computer-generated, often making certain situations very funny.
The soundtrack is fine, with some good tracks here and there. Often enough, the "no-enemy-around" music kept playing while the "fight" music activated while heading into battle, forcing me to completely remove the music from the game, to hear the competent but often cheap sound effects.
As far as I know, there is almost no replayability at all: no Steam or in-game achievements, difficulty settings, secrets or new game modes don't make me want to come back to this game.
Overall, I do appreciate that this game was made by only one person. But still, the repetitive combat, game-breaking glitches and frustration make this feel more like a chore than an epic fantasy. If you are really interested, pick it up on sale.
