Set one year after the events of Metro 2033, 21 year old Artyum must travel to the Botanical Gardens - home of the former Dark Ones' City to find a youthling to help restore the balance of power and to stop his nightmares about his choices from happening again. Were the Dark Ones really sent here to save us all, and is this the last of the Angels? I suppose you'll have to play the game to find out!
Metro: Last Light Redux is a technical update from the original game which features improved texture sizes and even some additional content as well as all DLC released for the original game. Almost anybody who isn't adeptly aware of everything in the game will more than likely not be able to distinguish the differences, and that's understandable.
I love this series and its other medium, It's based on a series of novels which tell the tale of Earth and mroe specifically Moscow Russia following the events of a Nuclear Winter. 2033 introduced us to this world, and one year later we have the events which unfold in Last Light. Where Khan finds a child of the race which Artyum foolishly destroyed, and it's up to Artyum to restore or destroy the balance for the next game.
The game has been updated, refined and developed by 4A, and it's developed by Russians based on a Russian story. The level of detail is such of that, that no two play-throughs are the same. I can say this confidently, as I really have lost count of how many times I've completed the series. The weapon choice is unique, diverse and generous, and you more than likely won't get to use every weapon in a single playthrough, The environments are the best part of the series, they're so immersive you could get lost and of you'd be fooling to not appreciate these environments.
It should also be noted that the available DLC for the most part ties in with the story directly, telling the events of certain situations happening as they happened through the perspective of other characters. This helps with the telling of the story, and naturally gives you insight to other key characters. Most DLC packages released fail in this respect to add value to a story or game, but simply layer information which was originally not planned into a title. The DLC in this case is worth playing once you've completed the game.

Right at the beginning you are provided with a book that actually contains the solutions to all the puzzles in the game. I actually found this a really interesting way to do a hint system, although less hint-y than outright solve-y. Nevertheless it is an 800+ page book filled with vast quantities of stuff. Despite this it is still reasonably easy to find the puzzles you are looking for if you get stuck (or just don't fancy faffing around with a bunch of gears again) whilst at the same time solutions to puzzles you haven't reached yet don't really stand out and spoiler themselves due to all the other info in there.
There are some points where your character will move from one place to another in sequences that are beautiful to watch the first time and then just rather annoying when you misclick and have to watch them wander back and fourth just to return you to where you already were. There are also a few times where clicking the exact right spot to get  your character to move/interact with something feels a little sticky and fair warning I did experience one crash however the game's save system meant I didn't lose any progress.
Overall though, the puzzles are beautifully done and mostly have some lovely ideas behind them, the story is charming and the art style is just incredible. It is relatively short (4-5 hours), which I think puts the price point rather high - I know I would have missed out on this had it not come up in a bundle and that would have been a shame. Although I normally have no problem saying a game is not worth picking up at full price, there is something about this one that makes me think that for a lot of people it probably will be.

L.A. Noire is a unique and special turn of events from the Rockstar formula. From cowboys and rolling the streets of imaginary universes commiting crime instead we are solving it. You play as Cole Phelps (Aaron Staton) in the city of L.A. as a police officer solving crimes. You play at a set of different desks, each desk with its own 'plot' so to speak which is comprised of many smaller cases. You'll solve cases for hours just to uncover the ending of your desk's plot.
The game holds no hands as you questions witnesses and perps while collecting evidence. You'll have to pay attention to your interrogatee's facial expressions and be aware of the evidence you've collected to either threaten or prove they are lying.

L.A. is a very large area to explore, but the time you'll spend will be mostly on time during cases. The content in this game is vast and more than worth your buck. It took me 27 hours to beat the whole game and I ignored street crimes. (I played this 100% the first time on PS3). L.A. is also the real L.A.! Companies and Cars are real. You can drive your grandpa's favorite cars and visit famous L.A. Landmarks. Actual companies are named including but not limited to Warner Brothers, Hughes, and Lockheed Martin in the cases you will solve.
The game is less about action and sandbox and more about the incredibly immersive story. You will grit your teeth and yell at your computer, "It's not him!", "You liar". I caught myself talking to myself, and to Phelps, many times.
You won't be disappointed in the story Rockstar was built for us.
Pros:
Neutral:
Cons:
I wholeheartadly recommend L.A. Noire for anyone passing buy with 20 bucks on hand. This is a Hollywood crime experience you shouldn't miss.

This game supposedly doesn't work for windows 10 users but after I upated my PC I never had any issues. Aside from that the game is amazing. I still haven't beat it, but I'm really close to the end and so far I love the story. It would seem like the gameplay would get repetative after a while but it's really not. The game constantly has you on the edge of your seat waiting to see where the case takes you next, and believe me, it takes you to some really unexpected places. The whole game revolves around searching crime scenes and various other places related to your current case for clues, interrogating various people, and the occasional fist fight, gun fight, or car chase.
This game will teach you right off the bat to pay close attention to detail and never rule anything out. You have you be very thorough with your investigations of crime scenes and anywhere else the game has you search (apartment buildings, bars, railroads, etc.) even the most minute things could be an important clue in helping you solve your case.
The interrogations are brought to life by the face caption which essentially puts a real actors face on a game characters body. This helps a lot because the main point of the interrogations is to read the suspects face to determine whether they are lying or not. This would be incredibly difficult to do with a game character's face. You have three options when interrogating someone, they will make their statement and you have to choose truth, doubt, or lie. Truth is pretty obvious, lie is for when you know they are lying and have proof of it, and doubt is for when you think they may be lying but don't have any solid evidence to back you up. Most of the time you can tell if people are lying because they will try to avoid making eye contact, fold their arms, shake their head a lot, etc. Essentially what someone does if they are actually lying to you in real life. You can also tell if they are lying by the way they speak, if they are lying they may stutter a lot, have a lot of voice cracks, or just generally speak in a higher pitched voice. And most of the time if they are telling the truth they will have no hesitation when they speak, they will maintain eye contact, etc.
The combat in the game is nothing special, it seems like it was ripped straight out of GTA. This isn't a bad thing because it's not the main focus of the game, and it's still pretty fun nonetheless. But again, nothing special.
The car mechanics can be somewhat tedious at times but for the most part it's just like any other game. Nothing new there.
There is a lot of sequences where you will find yourself chasing a suspect through a back alley or across rooftops. You can try to gun down the escapee, shoot into the air to scare them, or just try to get close and tackle them.
The city of L.A itself is very big and well designed. It looks really good and feels very alive. You can drive around for hours just enjoying the sights of L.A. There is also a lot of side missions and events to keep you entertained.
The story is really enjoyable, I don't want to spoil anything, and trust me, you don't want it spoiled for yourself. Just do your best to avoid spoilers and enjoy the story for yourself.
The game also has several platforming sections, but uh... we don't talk about those... best to just get them over with and then forget they ever happened in the first place...
That's about all I have to say. You should definitely buy this game if you're into detective stuff, or if you just want to have a fun experience.
Also, like I said earlier I had no problems launching the game, but if you do I know there is fixes for it. It is definitely worth it still to buy the game, even if you have to do some wonky stuff to get it to work.

That being said, I think that the game is definitely worth $20, even though it only lasts a few hours.

(For example: My Unfallen had a perk or tech (I can't remember where) which lets me force peace treaties on people. And then naturally I nagged them into trade and sceince treaties. Then alliances. Diplomantic Trees FTW!)
Shiny looking spaceships I can tweak and customize easily? Yep.
Pretty battles when I want to watch my creations blow the stuffing out of someone? Aye.
Addictive 'oh, I'm already up till 6am may as well take  one more turn' gameplay? Yeeeup.
Lovely soundtrack? Yes yes yes.
So, fun little 4X game, well worth picking up on sale.
Few bugs now and then (I've had a fleet vanish on me after taking a system and having to poke it a few times to get it to show back up again), but nothing game breaking.
Also, it took me a bit to realize, but each faction also has different numbers of slots on their ships.
For example, Riftborn Medium Hunter-class ships only have one single utility slot (For slapping in faster engines or whatnot), and unlike, say, the Sophen have no Weapon-Defense-Utility hardpoints...but fully upgraded they have something like seven+ weapon hardpoints. On the other hand, their Coordinater-class Medium ship has a ton of Utility hardpoints but only two weapon slots fully upgraded...so, you have to end up using the Coordinator with fleet speed boosters to get your actual killy ships anywhere in time.
On the other hand, when I played Sophen, EVERY ship was individually fast and had about the same amount of weapons.
It's a nice little touch.
Also, there's just something satisfying about watching a fleet battle and seeing your various ships roll the guns out to action stations. Riftborn literally detach them from the ship, Sophen all slide out of concealed ports, that sort of thing. Grand fun to watch.
Also, remember: Cravers are always, always antagonistic punks.
I'd also consider tagging Economic and Score victory off if you want to see some of the other event chains or victory types, because in the my experience, an alliance will tend to hit Economic Victory before it hits anything else.

I initially got this game because it was free and it looked cool,
After so long i still love this game, DE is a great company with regular updates and a lot of weapons and frames to collect and play with.
There is a separate currency in game which you can get using real money for,  but almost anything can be acquired through in game trading without having to make real money purchases.
The game does require you to grind a lot and I mean a lot, and there is a significant RNG factor to almost everything, you will be spending a significant chunk of your time praying to RNGesus to get the necessary drops,
The lore and story feels incomplete currently but if you poke into all the nooks and crannies you will find its rather rich and has a lot of potential a la dark souls.
It may get confusing in the early levels but you can always ask for help in chat, most players will be happy to help.
It also allows you to play as you want (within limits) want to be the guy that finishes missions without killing anyone? You can do that? Wanna only provide support and healing? You can do that. Wanna tear through hordes of enemies with your bare claws? You can do that.
The missions work in standard 4 person squads (there are special missions where you can have raids but that's for much later) you can have friends or you can join a public session or you can go solo.
There are different missions where youay have to protect something for a few waves, hack certain consoles to get data, kill a bunch of enemies or get people out of prisons and you can do this in a few ways.
The greatest part of the game is the customisation  of weapons and frames that allow you to make them feel like your own, you can always find a guide to get the best out of a weapon or frame but you are free to make a best that fits your playstyle instead.
Overall would recommend as something to put an hour everyday kinda game.

No bullcrap 10 shots from a tank to kill a single infantry unit.

The game has a very nice random factor added to it.

Although the gameplay is a bit slow-I might find it in myself to say that is a good thing.
Considering the large scale of the battlefields availble to you, it makes it much easier to manage things, even micro manage if you have a quick hand.
All in all this is a great game with many things for you to discover on your own.

This game was the cornerstone of my existence from March 2009 all the way until now. I have logged probably 2-3x the hours in this game than my entire Steam library combined, so I have no idea how many 1000's of hours I have played Halo Wars.
Halo Wars was released by Ensemble Studios in March 2009, the same developers that brought us the Age of Empires series, so if nothing else, you would know that Halo Wars was created by basically the grandfather of RTS games. I cannot remember when they began the project, but I believe it was somewhere between 2005-2007.
What people need to understand about the "limited" content is that it is a port from the Xbox 360, as such, Ensemble had to develop the game with the limits of the Xbox 360 in mind. So, let's go over some of the complants that people have.
-"My Scarabs are getting destroyed too easily."
Even though the Scarab is classifed as an "Uber" unit and it takes up 3000 of your resources + 20 out of your max 50 population as Covenant, the Scarab is not the be all end all of units and strategies in Halo Wars. A Scarab is just another vehicle and without the proper support it will get destroyed, as with all other strategies you must keep in mind what the enemy team and what your team is building and plan your military and strategy accordingly.
-"Scout vehicles are useless."
The 3 "Scout" units in the game are the UNSC's "Warthog," the Covenants "Ghost" and exclusive to the Brute Chieftain the "Chopper."
The Ghost, even though it has a research tree, is almost entirely useless after the first 5 minutes of the game. It is good only for killing un-upgraded scouts in the start of the game because they start with a weapon, unlike the Warthog and the chopper. Other than that, I have seen them maybe dodge a few Cobra shots or RPG's, but they take up too much room en masse and are not good at anything to supplement your army. It is best just to forget you can build them.
The Warthog does not start with a gun, though it does start with a ram ability. As you upgrade the Warthog you will add a turret, then a grenadier and finally you will replace the turret with a gauss turret. This is the only Scout unit in the game that I (personally) would incorporate into a full army, but only for a specific purpose. The Warthog is an extremely good supplement for taking out air units, though by themselves, they die pretty quickly, so it is not recommended to send them in to fight air alone, the air must be distracted by something else for the Warthogs to deal damage. Good in combination with Hawks or Hornets to fight Vampires or to get a slight edge on other air units.
The Chopper, you would see me using this more if they did not cost 2 population and were not in the Factory. Choppers are okay against light units, they take the least damage from their ram ability and have the best health of all the Scout units, but there are too many cons to create a Factory just to build Choppers (or anything for that matter with the exception of Locusts.)
-"When my partner(s) die (or leave) I don't get any of their population or other assests, so I can't continue the game."
Well yeah, you don't get anything of theirs, that's kinda the point. It's meant to be an extreme cripple when one of your allies is taken out, but that doesn't necessarily mean that the game's over for you. Depends on what the enemy has vs. what you have in terms of a military. Attack immeadiately, try to do the same thing they did to you to one of theirs and hopefully you'll balance the scales. I was in a game back on the 360 where both of my partners abandoned me in the first 30 minutes and it ended up being a 2v1 against me. That game lasted over 4 1/2 hours and I still won.
I could go on with this, but it already seems like this is getting too long for a review, so I'll stop here but if anybody has any questions, feel free to add me on Steam and ask away.

I have played on PVP Official servers for most of my 400 hours. I have found that whilst it is fun to raid people, it is not fun to be raided. You spend a lot of time building, particularly taming - hours in fact - on one dinosaur only for it to be killed within seconds. I then feel that pain and do not wish to raid others because of this. It is almost a rage-quitting factor to log on and see everything demolished and to find none of your loot has been taken - simply a clan has destroyed your base for the fun of it. I realize that is a part of the game, but not something I personally gain satisfaction from.
I also see the grind, especially as a solo play mostly, when it would take 6 hours in real life to tame one dino. Yes, you can get kibble, but the time it takes to acquire the dinos, to get the eggs, to make the kibble, basically equates far more than 6 hours in total. Meanwhile on a PVP server you would have been raided several times over, all to start at the beginning again.
You'll notice that I am critical of the PVP/Official Server gameplay, but this game in itself is awesome. I do understand if you're in a tribe of 15 it makes such gameplay elements are much easier and more achievable, but I do not believe the majority of the player base is a part of such consistant and friendly tribes. It's like pushing water uphill which is no fun at all, just a chore.
The game is still unoptimized, and laggy. Many say this is the Crysis of games in this time of gaming and the graphics and scope of the game make that understandable. It is almost breath taking, particularly on the Ragnarok map looking at the waterfalls and canyons. The creative imagination flows with the ideas of what to build in these amazing locations.... I could go on.
So, I rent my own server from
, password protected, PVE, 3x speed settings which I play with some family from time to time. That is enjoyable, far less of a grind, exploring at your own pace, without the fear of losing everything by the next login.
So, I do recommend this game for everyone to play. I would advise you should have a better graphics card to handle the game so it's more enjoyable; complaining it lags when you’re attempting to run the game with a toaster is ridiculous. I would advise that unless you're got a group of friends, PVP whilst an awesome concept, is a meaningless waste of time that you'll find on one login was all for nothing - that isn't a nice feeling. Don’t say I didn’t warn you!
Otherwise, a most excellent and enjoyable game. Get it when it's on discount however, $70 NZD is far too step in my opinion.

Halo Wars Definitive Edition is a timeless classic RTS game developed by Ensemble Studios and published by Microsoft Game Studios, taking place in the Halo universe. Players get to control all of the Halo universe enemies and hero's.

The player's gameplay of Halo Wars consists of building and controlling army's to destroy their opponents base, while defending their own. Players will construct structures and base's to produce a variety of units, such as tanks, Spartans, ODST squads, Grunts and Ghosts. Bases are locked locations with limited building zones, however can be upgraded to account for more buildings. Buildings include reactors, turrets, barracks, mortar pools, and aircraft stations. Halo wars plays like an RTS game but is restrictive in population and building locations. This doesn't take away from the RTS gameplay much, however may be frowned upon by hardcore RTS players.
The story of Halo Wars follows Sergeant Forge on his journey under the command of Captain Cutter. The story and gameplay of the campaign has variety and has been polished, but has a tendency to let they player camp down and wait without much backlash. The voice acting and visuals of the campaign are solid and fit well, and Halo Wars is a good looking game for its time. The campaign follows Forge on various planets fighting Covenant and other enemies, some of which include fungal life forms. Disappointingly, the Fungal Life forms are not a playable race.
Halo Wars Definitive Edition
does some things right:
•Fun skirmish and multiplayer
•Pretty well balanced
•Great looking game
•Campaign feels like halo
•Variety of campaign missions
•Good story
Halo Wars Definitive Edition does a few things wrong:
•Can turtle in most campaign missions
•Can win most matches by spamming a single unit type
•Skirmish AI can be dumb
•Decent but unpolished voice overs
•Lack of skirmish refining & feels unfinished
Overall, Halo Wars Definitive Edition is a classic and fantastic RTS game. To hardcore RTS fans, it may lack features other RTS games have, however this does not take away from the game at all. Halo Wars Definitive Edition belongs in every RTS, strategy, or Halo fans library.

L.A. Noire is a game developed by Team Bondi, an offshoot of Rockstar at the time it was made. People were up in arms about some of the conditions at the now shuttered studio in Australia. The head of development has responded to some of these claims. It doesn't seem that indifferent from much of the AAA landscape today. We'll just review the product here. Overall, the questionable management and terrible working conditions still produced one hell of a game about the 1940s Los Angeles era.
What you need to know is that on PC the game has been tremendously upgraded in the image quality department. 4K native is offered, but your best bet is 1080p with 4xSGSSAA through Nvidia Inspector, making this unique game a completely different experience compared to the PS3 version. This cannot be overstated.
In other regards, we don't have the upgraded audio from PS3. The shadows are better than the Xbox 360, but not as precise as the PS3. That might be a good thing as shadows in that game tended to be too sharp. Texture filtering bests both consoles. Overall, the cleanliness of the image is by far the most important aspect to enjoying and being immersed in the city.
As for controls: Going back to the PS3 version on the DS3 pad is exponentially worse than something like a DS4 and Input Mapper on PC. These two major changes make the PS3 version all but unplayable in retrospect. I actually went back to that version to compare, and the only thing I liked a tad more was the audio fidelity, though, it's not all that much better and most will not notice. The controls were abysmal in every way.
For the game, of course, we have vintage L.A. modeled with exquisite outer detail. The indoor locations are lacking outside of the story mode, and there isn't a lot to do in the city overall, but with the DLC there are plenty of story missions to investigate, and the varied nature of the game puts you in plenty of different parts of old time Los Angeles. Travelling by car is pretty fairly smooth, and finding all the different makes and models is actually worthwhile now that the graphics have proper AA and detail.
The action and movement is mediocre to okay. You won't be regarding this as the most fluid of shooting games, but what's there is serviceable if a little routine at times. Side missions are fairly bare bones. Collectibles are hard as hell to find in this sprawling map. The investigations to me are very fun, and I actually think they still hold up today. I know some people criticize the lack of knowing what to do in certain situations, but I still think this game comes closest to being one of the only immersive detective-style games out there.
The Lie-Doubt-Truth mechanic works because it's honestly quit fun roaming for clues, and the art direction inside the various homes and building you enter is fairly top notch stuff even by modern standards. Being in 1940s L.A. is just kind of fun when it comes down to it. If this is not your type of setting, and you expect super high quality action, I would probably skip this game.
The audio and voicework is quite good for the most part. Animations in the faces hold up because of the work they put into it, though, that does hamper the port at only 30FPS. There is a widescreen fixer for 60FPS, but I personally choose to have SGSSAA over the extra 30FPS, which can look a bit wonky at times. It is a lot smoother with that fix, so it is there if you need it.
Most of what you get out of this game depends on if you like the setting. The stories and characters are for sure a cut above the average game, and some of them are very well done. But it comes back down to if you like this period and if you have the PC to play it right. An OC'd 970 and 2500K should do the job. I am currently using a 1070 and it runs perfectly at 30FPS with SGSSAA at 4x.
So it's worth it just to see the detail of the city and the 1940s. The artists here pull it all off with great abandon. So much detail was drawn into this city, and yes it is a shame there is not more to do. Sometimes development hell gets the best of you. Still, the stories are interesting enough and the locations all now look so much more lovely than they ever did on the consoles. Travel around and chill out with L.A. Noire's gritty take on vintage crime and you'll have a fun experience for 30 hours or so.

So I have 66 hours logged in Warframe. That's not really that much, but I've played enough to give a decent review.
First, I wanna say that overall, the game is pretty fun. It's pretty much a 3D space ninja hack n slash. While it does end up being quite grindy, the game world itself is super interesting. The graphics are pretty crisp and the game runs well on my PC.
In the game, everything is accessable from your personal space drop ship. This is more or less the lobby where you can join games and craft items. You can customize the interior and get new ships. Personally, sometimes when I don't even feel like playing a match, I'll just sit in my cool♥♥♥♥♥space cruiser and listen to Ordis and the Lotus chime in.
You start off with a choice from 3 warframes. I started with Volt. Choose wisely, because you will be playing this warframe for a bit before you get your next one. I finally crafted Oberon after 66 hours logged.
My favorite aspect of the game is just the map design and visuals. Each map seems like it's randomly generated to an extent. There are always cool little pathways and hidden passages through the spacey-scifi themed maps. Like, the map design is quite amazing, tbh. Each planet you go to has it's own scenery. It's really cool.
What I don't like about Warframe is that it's very grindy. Missions more or less repeat themselves. There are quests that follow somewhat of a storyline, but other than that it's a grind. The game starts off relatively easy. You progress through each planet of the solar system, starting with Earth. Each planet has several maps that you must complete before you can access the junction to the next planet. You have to fulfill a few requirements before being able to cross to the next planet, such as opening 3 grineer caches on Uranus. Some of these requirements can be tricky, and nothing is really explained in Warframe. So expect to be googling how to find the caches. I still haven't found all 3....and honestly, I think this may be the point where I quit playing Warframe. I just want to get to the next planet, but this stupid quest is preventing me. It's not even a difficult quest, it's just time consuming running back and forth through one map looking for these insanely hidden caches.
The weapons are cool. I feel like I end up using melee most often as Volt. Reloading guns takes way too long, and I waste mod space by adding faster reload times. Melee is just a good bash-em-up. If you are playing for free, then you only get a few weapon slots. Meaning, you can only have a few weapons in your inventory. So if you want to craft another weapon, you have to sell one. You have to buy more weapon slots with Platinum.
The characters and voice acting in the game are super cool. I love how there are all these factions. CLEM. GRAKATA. You really feel like you're in this world.
This game is not pay-to-win. The things you can purchase with money are all cosmetic items. The only thing I feel like you'd want to pay for is extra weapon slots. You could play this game to the point of exhaustion and not have to pay a cent to get ahead. It'll just take some time.
All in all, I recommend this game. Check it out. If anything, feel the power of a zippy space ninja.

L.A. Noire's absorbing investigations and intoxicating sense of Noir style make it an unforgettable journey through the seamy side of the City of Angels.
L.A. still had streetcars in 1947, but it was a city quickly becoming dominated by the automobile, and that's the only way to travel in L.A. Noire. Thankfully, driving is fun.
The gunplay is very easy to pick up. You can hide behind cover, and pop out to squeeze off shots.
L.A. Noire isn't all about badgering people, though. This is still an open-world game. You're free to deviate from a case, explore faithfully recreated 1947 Los Angeles, and tackle more action-oriented missions. No, you can't run wild like in Grand Theft Auto (you're a cop, accept it), but there are some other things to do. Forty "unassigned cases" come in as calls on the radio.
Gunfights, foot chases, car chases, and the occasional simple brawl don't just spring up during cases. They're also a regular part of the street crimes that are reported over the radio, which you can choose to respond to or ignore. The voice acting is good and the visual face effect when someone is tense after telling a lie, is brilliant made.
The  game has car chases, gunfights, and a point-tally to judge the quality of your police justice, but it's a slow-paced, meditative experience. The focus isn't on how good you are at scoring headshots with a pistol but instead your ability to read a suspect's face and determine if he or she is telling the truth, holding something back, or flat out lying.
I felt that even if the  game had  21 cases, some of which can take more than an hour to complete, L.A. Noire drags at times because it recycles the same drama and you cant help feeling a sense of Deja Vu. There's an omniscient narrator in the early missions of L.A. Noire who disappears halfway through and never returns. I also felt that Phelt story was forcefully told and often too hasty and in bits so you never get the whole picture about his personality or his past.

I have been in and out of this game since meeting one of the level designers back in beta. And I have to say that it is quite possibly the best HL2 mod I have ever played. I would even go as far to say it the best mod to any game, and I love both Killing Floor and Alien Swarm.
The objective based gameplay is something you just don't see enough of these days and the variation in objective design is fantastic. The 3 class system is well balanced and the weapon/implant selection is fantastically varied without having any real automatic 'I WIN' equipment.
The metaspace/cyberspace split has been well executed, with the meatspace maps being generally well laid out, and the cyber maps freedom of movement and physics application being something I've not truly witnesses elsewhere. Both realms rely one each other to either create vulnerabilities in their opponents (like hacking enemy turrets or opening new attack paths) or protecting from weakesses (shutting off poison gas or protecting the defenseless host body while someone hacks). The teamwork potential in the game is incredibly high and most of the time I find its something pubs just naturally fall into without a lot of instruction. This could just be the playerbase the mod attracts, but I've never seen this kind of intricate natural teamwork form anywhere (the closest being TF2 but thats mostly 'stick together, oh we need a medic', not exactly complex)
The only thing truly missing at this point is the graphical style is starting to get a bit dated, but considering it came out a decade ago it still holds up a heck of a lot better than most games from that time. They captured the 'dystopian' cuberpunk aspect really well, with the two factions posessing a unique look and the locations matching the objectives and the universe well.
You should play this, at least a few hours. Get some friends together, or try and find a populated pub server. The fact this mod went so unnoticed is a tragedy, and I feel it had great potential to become a new CS or at least have a standalone release like Killing Floor did.

This is a flawed masterpiece and one of my absolute favourites along with GTA, Max Payne and Mafia 2.
L.A. Noire's absorbing investigations and intoxicating sense of Noir style make it an unforgettable journey through the seamy side of the City of Angels.
L.A. still had streetcars in 1947, but it was a city quickly becoming dominated by the automobile, and that's the only way to travel in L.A. Noire. Thankfully, driving is fun.
The gunplay is very easy to pick up. You can hide behind cover, and pop out to squeeze off shots.
L.A. Noire isn't all about badgering people, though. This is still an open-world game. You're free to deviate from a case, explore faithfully recreated 1947 Los Angeles, and tackle more action-oriented missions. No, you can't run wild like in Grand Theft Auto (you're a cop, accept it), but there are some other things to do. Forty "unassigned cases" come in as calls on the radio.
Gunfights, foot chases, car chases, and the occasional simple brawl don't just spring up during cases. They're also a regular part of the street crimes that are reported over the radio, which you can choose to respond to or ignore. The voice acting is good and the visual face effect when someone is tense after telling a lie, is brilliant made.
The  game has car chases, gunfights, and a point-tally to judge the quality of your police justice, but it's a slow-paced, meditative experience. The focus isn't on how good you are at scoring headshots with a pistol but instead your ability to read a suspect's face and determine if he or she is telling the truth, holding something back, or flat out lying.
I felt that even if the  game had  21 cases, some of which can take more than an hour to complete, L.A. Noire drags at times because it recycles the same drama and you cant help feeling a sense of Deja Vu. There's an omniscient narrator in the early missions of L.A. Noire who disappears halfway through and never returns. I also felt that Phelt story was forcefully told and often too hasty and in bits so you never get the whole picture about his personality or his past.

Lumino City is primarily a puzzle game with some point-and-click adventure elements. The game relies heavily on its visual appeal and indeed, the hand-made sets look delightfully colorful, and overall the game has a charming atmosphere.
There is a coherent backstory, too, but it doesn't get in the way of the gameplay. Instead, little clues are spread throughout the world, and all the pieces are tied together during the ending credits. Be sure to stick around for that!
The gameplay is fairly simple. You play as Lumi, who explores the City in search of her grandfather. In practice that means figuring out how to move from one screen to the next, which often requires talking to some people, finding a key to open a lock, and so on. However, this part of the game is fairly simple, and the main challenge of the game is solving its 34 puzzles.
The puzzles are a mix of visual and logic puzzles, and are generally entertaining, though not all of them are very inspired. Some concepts get recycled a few times, while in other cases the puzzle is more easily solved by trial-and-error than by logical thinking. There is one puzzle which relies heavily on memorization, others require diligent application of look-up tables. If you get stuck, there is an in-game manual where you can look up their solutions. I didn't need it on my playthrough, but I peeked in after the fact, and was disappointed to see that the manual immediately spoils the complete solution instead of providing hints. That seems like a wasted opportunity.
At $20, the price is a little high for a game that should take around 6 hours to finish, especially since it has little replay value. Those who are on a budget should wait for a sale. That being said, the game itself is well worth your time.

Halo Wars on steam is a great idea. More classics that were previously locked into specific consoles should come to PC and should come to a platform that is used by a large number of people, such as Steam. But having played RTS games for many hours I cannot recommend this game. The features that would be considered standard, such as grouping and high unit diversity, are not here. If you are looking to relive some nostalgia with some friends and don't know too much about RTS games this will be a good fit. But the clunky unit collision that will stop units from moving in an open field, the lack of units and unit types, and the extreme simplicity of this game make it not up to par with the standard of RTS games today. Again, if you want to relive some childhood memories go for it. But after playing it myself I realize that some games should remain in your memory under a shroud of nostalgia. More classic IP's on Steam would be great, but hopefully they get some games that stand the test of time.

While it's easy to see why 2K Games wanted to remaster the first Bioshock game, it comes as an even bigger surprise that they also decided to revamp Bioshock 2; the game was already well advanced for its time, not only in gameplay but in visuals as well. Even though Bioshock 2 Remastered doesn't come with the same hefty assortment of problems that plagued Bioshock Remastered, it still comes with a whopping amount of problems that diminishes its enjoyability.
It's safe to say that Bioshock 2 Remastered does look stunningly better than its older version; the water, reflections, and dynamic lighting most notably. The title is even more beautiful in the Remastered edition than the first Bioshock Remastered is, there's a massive visual difference between the two games. Once again, however, aesthetics are the only upgrade that Bioshock 2 has seen, and all previous ailments of the game still prove to be problematic; along with a new set of issues to boot.
First of all, crashing. If you've read my Bioshock Remastered review, you will know that these Remastered editions committing suicide constantly is a huge problem; Bioshock 2 Remastered is no different, although I found that this game actually crashes less. Unlike the first game, you can actually save and open the map screen without fear of the game taking a massive dump. It more or less enjoys crapping out while attempting to boot the game up.
Since we're currently talking about new problems, let's talk achievements. Multiple achievements are bugged right now, with three being absolutely unattainable; if you're going for Rapture Historian like I was, you're SOL until if and when 2K decide to release a fix. So if you've already collected the audio diaries in the original Bioshock 2, don't worry about it here unless you really don't care about achievements. The same goes for Master Researcher, and finding all of the Power to the People stations. While those achievements are completely broken, ones such as Master Gatherer, Master Hacker, most of the other hacking related trophies, Big Spender, and an assortment of others require tricks to unlock.
Now, on to older problems. I'm happy to say that Bioshock 2 didn't have as many original problems as Bioshock did, but there is one prevalent issue that still infests the Remastered edition. Every now and then, especially when transitioning into and back out of water, your left arm which hosts your Plasmids disappears. There's no way to get it back without reload trial and error, dying, running into a section where Eleanor speaks to you, or attempting to inject an Eve Hypo; the latter of which doesn't always work.
It's really a sad state of affair that 2K Games have butchered the Bioshock 1 and 2 Remastered editions as badly as they have. There's zero reason for these titles to crash so often, and to have the same problems that they were ported with back in 2007 and 2010 respectively. While Bioshock 2 Remastered is less problematic than its predecessor, I still cannot give it a recommendation over its original title. However, I am happy to say that they removed the awful multiplayer portion from the Bioshock 2 Remastered version, so that's a plus in my book. When, and if, 2K decide to revise these problems, I will update my review. Until then, just play the original versions of both games.

Youtubers Life is essentially a time management RPG that reminds me of Game Dev Tycoon. You create your character, and you start in a house with your character’s mother where you have to balance between hunger, sleep (Both of which contribute to your ability to have good ratings on your videos), studying (A’s and B’s get money from your mother), friends (I’m not sure what they do for you yet except eventually lead to collaborations; More ratings), work (Direct cash that doesn’t come from YT’s monetization), and several other things that may not be readily apparent at the beginning.
The whole time you can purchase upgrades to your PC which allows for stronger videos. You even have to edit videos which acts as a miniature puzzle game, as connecting all the modules will lead to a better video and thus, more views and subscribers.
It’s a neat part of the game that I can appreciate.
Another part that reminds me of Game Dev Tycoon, is that you’re not stuck in your mother’s house forever. At a certain subscriber limit, you’re asked to become roomates with someone. Drop some cash, and you move out, and it comes with a few perks. Your fridge is closer, though you have to buy your own food (Which are usually cheap in comparison). The need to study is replaced with online courses to improve your abilities, which is completely optional but costs money. You don’t get the occasional 50$ from your mother but at this stage of the game (A couple hours in), you’ll be making more from your videos anyway.
Would I recommend it? It’s a neat little fantasy to have your custom made self playing games for money. It’s still in Early Access so there’s a few things missing. To be fair, there’s a full game here. It’s a Simulator where you manage time and resources so if that’s your thing, go for it.

Но вместо того, чтобы объединить усилия, города-станции погрязли в борьбе за абсолютную власть и устройство судного дня с армейских складов D6. Назревающая гражданская война может навсегда стереть человечество с лица Земли. В роли Артема, отягощенного виной, но движимого надеждой, вы владеете ключом к выживанию – лучом надежды в этот темный час
✔Metro: Last Light Redux – самая лучшая и полная версия классической игры Metro: Last Light, обновленная с применением последней, самой совершенной версии графического ядра 4A Engine для игровых систем последнего поколения.
✔Игроки, не знакомые с серией, получат один из лучших сюжетных шутеров за всю историю жанра – эпическое приключение, сочетающее в себе захватывающий «Сурвайвл-хоррор», исследование местности, тактические бои и стелс. В это издание входит также весь выпущенный ранее загружаемый контент, который добавляет дополнительные 10 часов к игре в одиночном режиме.
✔Поклонники игры в ее исходном виде заметят, что механика улучшилась, и появилось новое –например, возможность в любой момент узнать время и боезапас, а бои и фигуры игровых персонажей заново анимированы.

If you're okay with finding ways to work around horrible framerate (changing resolution back and forth for me) and an fps cap of 30, you'll find a great game in L.A. Noire. This game is really unique. You get thrown around into every police department, which keeps cases fresh. From homicide to arson, you always have a big case to solve. The face capturing is the best I have ever seen. It's so accurate that you'll recognize many actors' faces. I found it very challenging and rewarding when correctly interrogating suspects. As someone who searches around for treasures and such in games like Uncharted and Bioshock, I enjoyed looking for clues, many of which are well hidden. The DLC is a great edition, with awesome side missions like Nicholson Electroplating and Reefer Madness. The driving is kind of bland, but the 1940s L.A. map is huge and the hidden cars were a nice touch. Plus you can have your partner drive you everywhere if you want. I also found it nice to place a Rockstar game with historically real places, vehicles, criminals, and social paradigms. There are even fictionalized versions of real crimes like the Black Dahlia Murder (which you actually get to solve). Overall, the cinematic feel, great acting and gameplay made L.A. become one of my favorite games. If you're really into mid-19th century film noire, you can even put the game in black and white. Pick up the complete version during the next steam sale.

Of similar games I have reviewed I can find a few endearing qualities in Lumino City. Defnitely not worth 15 quid.
1. The artwork is pretty innovative, cut out folded card and paper people make for a pleasing effect simple and clean only spoiled by the out-of-focus backgrounds which caused me some amount of eyestrain.
2. A likeable story idea and main character development kicks in right at the start, you learn how to play Lumino City in stages, however the learning gets a bit slow when all of the dialog becomes repetitive.
3. Grandad drops a hand manual, and it's probably more fun browsing the diagrams in the Handymanual which is in reality useless, than to ply the game. I found the manual quite fun.
4. Sound track, yep flawless, sets the mood and works, but not enough to swing it when frustration sets in.
1. Every puzzle is not supplied with much of a "what am I supposed to do" hint at all, for example the lemons puzzle is confusing since the "lemon-battery prongs" are labelled + and - but the labels have no actual relevance at all.
2. When a puzzle makes no sense, brute force will solve it - and brute force clicking about on the screen in order to pick up some random item which hides in plain sight was not something I found "gameplay" enhancement.
3. When one of the quests to open a can involves going back and forth between 2 neighbours 5 times over playing messenger-person, it gets a little bit thin, they are neighbours after all. I gave up after the only 2 acceptable puzzles which involved light and seemed to make the game interresting, only to be followed by more drudgery.
Sorry, but maybe for a £1.70 pricetag, this might be a keeper, but since I paid less on a bundle I'm not done out of pocket anyway. Worth playing only for the graphics.

Warframe is a horde shooter RPG with a large number of creative weapons, abilities, and mission objectives. It is F2P with microtransactions, including the most well-done cosmetic system of any game I have personally played. It has fun, agile gameplay which other studios are only attempting to mimic with limited results, years after Warframe's release. It also has a creative and inspired storyline, albeit one that Digial Extremes purposely hides details of (to encourage player speculation). Additionally, for a game of this size, it is incredibly bug-free (except for the Jordas Verdict, ♥♥♥♥ that). However, this game is not without its flaws.
Again, the greatest strengths of Warframe are is its creativity and customizability, be it builds, choices of weapons, or cosmetic design, and its fluid movement and aiming system. Digital Extreme's work here is nothing short of incredible, and you'll have to play the game to understand what I mean.
My two flaws with the game revolve around enemies. Firstly, enemy design generally lacks depth. In the Grineer faction for example, a vast majority of normal units possess hitscan or homing weapons. To make the game interactive, DE adds an accuracy limit to enemies, causing them to miss more against faster-moving targets. I feel like this is a "band-aid" style of design and should simply be remedied by the introduction of enemies with non-hitscan attacks. Secondly, enemy power generally scales in an uncreative fashion similar to Diablo 3, where health, armor, and damage levels of the same enemy types simply increase towards infinity as you progress.
Lastly, there are multiple small flaws, such as the attainability of orokin catalysts for new players, or the inconsistency of no-scoping on a sniper rifle. I feel like these are small errors that should be made known to Digital Extremes and improved upon.
By and large though, this remains my favorite RPGs on steam and one of my favorite games of all time. With over 1.6k hours clocked into the game and over $1000 happily spent to support the game, I think it speaks for itself. Happy hunting!

I sunk about 300-400hr in that game and let me assure you that it was all worth it. The game was my gate way to 4x and certainly satisfy my need for daily dose of space opera; but it was known that the game has always had flaws. The art department was certainly one of them. Sometime it was enough to keep me from playing United Empire where its emperor look like someone took a picture from deviant art. The factions were kind of meh with at least 3 human factions that kind of similar to each other. There were no memorable moments except for when you first saw the space battle and that was it. Truth to be told I was content with the game at the time and maybe 2 weeks ago, before I got this ♥♥♥♥ing gem.
HOLYMOLLY how much did Sega pour into this guy? I mean the fact that AMPLITUDE got themselves acquired by big AAA publisher was certainly not a good news. Looking back what they did to Total War definitely worry some die hard fan of the studio because of some devious business decisions. But that was another story, from another franchise. This one is not that kind of dumb down or cash cow whatsoever. This is art asset push to eleven, music put to Horatio out of 10 and gameplay+narrative improvement that would make the God Emperor of Man cry himself to his eternal slumber.
EVERYTHING has been improved. From the UI, which surprisingly enough was actually pretty good in the first game and what they did was to adjust some minor detail; to the factions that have been completely revamp. United Empire (beware the alien, the mutant, the heretic) is now truly the imperialist that you know and love for their traits from both the good old vaulters and those hippy guys from the first game. Sophons are now adorable science guys with terrifying late game potential. Next are the Vodyani with their weird colonization, hard to play but rewarding if master. Lumeris – T H I C C mafia in space, nuff said. Unfallen, tree people who come to life thank to the community; this is also one the thing that I appreciate the dev, they are no doubt, still passionate about their game. Riftborn with their also weird bubble thingy. And craver for, well, craver. Still hate playing next to those bugs. Horatio is perfect, as always.
Bottom line once more time: This game is everything fans would hope for. It live up to the hype (if any, their marketing department still leave a lot to be desired) and it deliver with stunning beauty. Art design, art design, art design; they took their lesson from both Endless Space, Endless Legend and combine the elegant of the latter to the efficient and minimalist design of the former. It totally delivers. The quest system in addition to the improvement of the resource management fresh the living s h it out of the gameplay. It makes the game feel alive, and the good thing is that there would be more to come. AMPLITUDE has been chunked out free DLC like mad. Those guys f u cks, and they know their fans as well.

Endless Space 2 is a fun, relaxing 4X strategy game that has you carving out your place in the galaxy, cooperating with and competing against the other inhabitants as depending on your playstyles.
Pros:
-Sci-Fi theme is extremely well executed with plenty of detail and lore for everything involved, from the completely different way species play to the randomly generated galaxies and solar systems.
-While rich in user choice and micromanagement customary to this style of game, ES2 has a UI and GUI that is extremely intuitive, helpful, clean, and functional. I was able to pick it up with minimal fussing about in the tutorials.
-There are a multitude of random events and quests that sometimes respond to how you operate your empire, from being aggressive and warlike to peaceful and diplomatic. Taking the place of a dedicated storyline or campaign, a primary faction quest is supplemented by these random quests as well as the procedurally generated galaxy and randomly placed enemies to force you to select the best option for your empire each time. This means what worked well in one game, say, being warlike and picking a military option for your quest, won't necessarily work in another, where the enemies are much stronger and the only way you can compete is, say, economically. Replayability is greatly enhanced, because by the end of each game your faction could be completely unrecognisable from another through bonuses, specialisation, and intergalactic political alliances.
-Fantastic engagement with the player base has meant ES2 is a quickly evolving game that is responding to feedback and polls by introducing entire patches and free DLCs to expand functionality, depth, and replayability.
-You can create your own factions to suit your playstyles, although the editor feels somewhat restrictive.
-Turn-based gameplay and amazing soundtrack create a very calming atmosphere that is enjoyable to unwind with for a couple hours.
-Frankly, it looks amazing. Seriously. Graphics, textures, effects, battles, scenery, GUI, spaceships... this game is a visual treat at all levels.
Cons:
-ES2 is not without flaws. The constant updates by the developers has meant that with all the new content updates, a large amount of bugs, save corruptions, and crashes have tagged along. The developers are responding quickly, however, and are markedly improving the game's performance and stability. Expect a buggy game for now, but know it is because the developers are taking the time and energy to add functionality and essentially free DLCs based on player feedback and wishes. (not kidding, they have polls and competitions all the time)
-The enemy AI is not great- diplomacy is all over the map and they are still entirely outmatched by a decent human player in combat. I'd argue its better than a CIV AI, but it could feel somewhat subjective without seeing how the code actually works.
-The different factions, while fun and adding to replayability, begin to feel stale after a while, especially if you play single-player only or favour a particular playstyle. Expect to spend time creating your own factions after you get tired of winning as Unfallen fifty-seven games in a row.
-Spaceship battles are pretty boring. Even the limited involvment you had in ES1 through real-time battle cards has been shunted to battle setup, so all space battles are essentially cinematic cutscenes rendered in-game. Beautiful but you cannot effect any changes during battles.
In Conclusion, Endless Space 2 is a fantastic game, and most of its flaws are either being actively worked on by the development team or a result of the genre of game it represents. I highly recommend it to any sci-fi gamers, those looking for a relaxing turn-based strategy game, or fellow travellers in the CIV series or Anno line.

At this time I've put in 36 hours to the Metro Last Light regular campaign. I can't recommend the Redux edition of Last Light to anyone who already has all the DLC for normal Last Light. The engine is the same so its still the same game. I heard there were sections of the game where you could go and explore parts of the world that weren't there before, though I made a point of exploring the regular edition and tried doing the same with the game (currently just past Venice in the campaign) and I haven't found any new parts of the world so far. Though they could have meant Metro 2033 Redux, I'll review that separately when I've played it.
I will however completely recommend this game to people who have either bought Last Light normal, and not bought any of the DLC, or people who haven't bought the game before in any form. (5/10) Lack of true innovation for the redux version of Last Light (when compared to Normal, this is not the final score, just what I give it compared to the normal edition)
For the actual game and not the Redux vs Normal section of the review.
The game is set around post-apocolyptic Russia where nuclear devastation has wiped out alot of people.
Thus you go through the game trying to make moral decisions wether to kill people, help people, or just be on your way.
Choices you make will have an effect one way or another later down the road. I'll list the negatives first.
The game has a confusing stealth system that I haven't really figured out yet, so that makes stealthing slightly unpredictable and occasionally frustrating. When enemy AI see you when they shouldn't, are hard to shake off your trail (once they see you its like they always know where you are) but if you're in a shadow you can sometimes sit right in front of them and they won't find you.
They do have a lack of voice actors in the game which isn't a big deal because the storytelling and immersion make up for it, but it still can get on your nerves from time to time (keep in mind they made this game in Ukraine and had to smuggle in computers to try and work on this game, they were hampered by the country they inhabit)
Thats about it for the negative parts of the review.
Now for the good stuff.
The game has amazing graphical quality, most of the textures are really good, even in places you wouldn't necessarily look. The lighting quality is amazing and all the monsters are very well detailed.
The guns all feel solid, and while some of the monsters are bullet sponges, the gun still feels like it will do the job, and I never had the feeling that my bullets weren't registering.
Interestingly enough, occasionally you will be given puzzles, not all monsters can be killed with bullets, and once you figure out how that works, the fight becomes a whole lot shorter and much more satisfying, espeically when you feel like you're outsmarting the Devs and the Monster by conquering a big rough-tough monster without firing one single bullet the entire fight.
The story is good, though it may tend to branch out and try and create too many side stories near the end it still helps with the immersion
did I mention immersion? Everything in this game draws you into the world and makes you feel like you're a part of it, from trying to remember to keep your flashlight charged and filters stocked up, to the high standard of graphics acheived, to the immersive storytelling from the part of the random characters you meet in the world, it all feels like you're not some big awesome dude out to save the planet, but just part of a system and you were in the right place at the right time.
Final little side note before I give the rating, Listen to the AI, they will tell you things and you will learn so much more about the story and world that you inhabit, plus you'll be much less confused, (and explore, every side door you find, GO IN IT!)
Final rating is still a 9-10/10   If you're bugged by the stealth system and the lack of varied voice actors in the game, its the 9/10, if you don't care about that, its 10/10 for good storytelling, immersive environement, and good graphics!

Be prepared to spend a few months of your life...  You will die, and die a lot!
This game is addicting, highly skill based with a steep learning curve to master but easy to learn.  And nothing will prepare you for the satisfaction and sensation of making your first kill and making your enemies head explode.
This game is unlike any game you think you have played before, unless you played the HL2 mod Age of Chivalry.  Chivalry is a real time swing trace control system that allows lots of possibilities for attack combos and enough weapon and class variations that you will be able to find something that fits your play style.
This game is highly skill based.  There is no powering up, no buying weapons, no magic or fantasy BS.  It is straight up medieval warfare, Hollywood style.  There are many different game modes and mods with lots of custom maps.
Game Modes:
TO = Team Objective - Two factions, Mason (Red) and Agatha (Blue) that are battling for control over ancient lands.  You will be working together to defend or attack, castles, villages, sea ports, kidnapped Kings and much more.
TD = Team Death match - Two factions, Mason (Red) and Agatha (Blue) battle to the death where the only ojective is to the first team to reach 50 kills.  Death to your enemies!
LTS = Last Team Standing - Two factions, Mason (Red) and Agatha (Blue) battle to the death except each player only gets one life per round and there are 7 rounds per match.   There can be only ONE!
CTF = Capture the Flag - Two factions, Mason (Red) and Agatha (Blue), traditional capture enemies flag and bring it back to your spawn
FFA = Free for ALL -  This is every man for himself and everyone is your enemy but you are allowed to play anyway you want, you can even team up with friends and take on the entire server if you wish or fight solo against everyone.  There can be only ONE!
Duel = Duel Mode - this is a structured mode where it is truly 1 vs 1 and you get to pick you fight and anything goes.  The best 2 out of 3 rounds.  Two man enter, One man leaves.
TO2 - Horde Mode - This is Coop play against an ever increasing number of Hord bots.  As each round ends you can buy various weapons and armor.  How many levels and waves of the horde can you stand against?
Modded Game Modes:
INFECTION - This is a moded coop mode were the first person to die becomes the infected and when you die you become the infected till there is only one left.
MERCS/BALANCEMOD - These are competitive custom rebalances of the game that attempts to balance certain classes.  It also restores 1st hit flinch and other minor tweaks.  BalanceMod adds the ability to parry projectiles and even arrows.  These are typically hosted servers by the competitive community for more organized scrimmages and tournaments.
WARMOD – Another rebalance of the game but this adds in more directional parring, and weapon clashing so if the weapons have collision boxes and cannot be penetrated.  Shields have also been improved
GIANTSLAYERS – This is a FFA mod but for every kill you grow bigger and more powerful to the point of you becoming a giant and just stomp your enemies.  It is played on regular maps
LASERSWORD – This a basically a Star Wars rip off with lots of SW based maps but using Chivalry fight mechanics.
BLACKKNIGHT – Monty Python black knight mode where your arms and limbs can be cut off but you can still hobble around and fight, lots of laughs.
JUGGERNAUT - First player to get a kill becomes the Juggernaut, an oversized player with extra strength and health.  Kill the juggernaut to become the juggernaut.
SUPER SMASH BROTHERS – This is an FFA mode that increases damages and blow back as well as double jumping.  Lots of fun and silliness.
When you first start playing, you will die and die a lot!  Play the tutorial first as that will give you a basic understanding of the different classes, weapons and some tactics.  Then hop in an FFA server and start unlocking you weapons.  Be prepared to play at least a month before you get all your weapons unlocked and begin to get a real understanding of the game.
Duel mode is great for mastering the 1v1, FFA is great for mastering the 1v many and TO is really where it all comes together.    Team Objective maps are where all your skills and team work come into play.  Military tactics and strategies really come in handy when sieging a castle or raiding a village, defending against the onslaught of field artillery  like catapults, ballista, trebuchets, battering rams and siege towers filled with your enemy.
On the technical side, the game is very ping dependent as well and GPU and CPU intensive.  If you have a low level PC, plan on turning down/off many of the graphic special effects that make it look so beautiful so that you will have decent FPS.  Make sure you join the lowest ping servers you can as the game timing gets radically different as your ping increases or the ping gap between players increases, missing hits and parries, ghost swings, and getting hit out of range become more prevalent the higher the pings
There are plenty of instructional videos for improving your game and plenty of servers to get your medieval game on.  The higher ranked players and clans will usually help you get better along the way if you just ask and be willing to take their advice if you want to "get gud"  But be prepared to get roasted and or vote kicked if you start team killing or doing other stupid things.  Time in game, patience, and practice will gain you experience that will be your greatest reward.   But it will not be easy.  There are a few over powered classes and several minor bugs here and there that can be frustrating at times but far from game breaking.  There will be things that you will see that will make you see exploits where none exist but as your skill increases and your ability to deal with different situations and improvise battle and combat strategies, you will discover that you becoming a master.
Can you make it to the upper levels of game play?  Are you ready and up for the challenge?  Then come get some!

An absolutely beautiful example of what a PC game can look like. The textures & models are pretty good, however the lighting is just beautiful and environmental effects add a great deal to the world. This may easily well be the best looking game I have ever played. Perhaps finally besting Crysis.
You have to manually charge the battery that powers your light every now & then, replace the filter on your mask, along with a whole bunch of other little things that make the game just that much more immersive. But none of these little things ever feel like they're in the way, if anything they add an element of immersion I wish other developers would bother to put in their games.
The guns feel great and there's not one to date that's felt as good to let off some rounds. Each has about 3-4 customization options from stocks and scopes to different barrel tips among other weapon specific components.
The human AI can be a bit janky at times and a bit stupid but mutants are intelligent and you'll spend plenty enough time fighting them to keep things interesting. At launch of the origional, I come across maybe 2-3 bugs through the whole game, one of them forced a checkpoint restart. Though checkpoints are hardly more than 10 minutes apart so it's not an issue at all, as there were barely any bugs in the first place.
The world is mostly linear but often allows for some exploration after about two to three hours into the game. If they were to make a Fallout-esq open world game in this world that wasn't so story driven it could easily be game of the decade worthy.
The story is alright, the world is interesting, and occasionally you'll encounter the game's horror element which does indeed go beyond creepy mutants crawling about. Though in the end, I have pretty much no issue with the game at all aside from it holding your hand too long at the start.
All in all, its certainly worth the $45 I paid and I encourage you to play ranger mode even if you're new.

I bought this game a long time ago, but I haven't played it then. Few days ago I finally decided to check it out and the game charmed me. It has really amazing cabaret/noir style atmoshpere and awesome matching music. Gameplay itself is pretty innovative too. You need to switch between 3D and 2D mode platformer. It is very interesting that in the 2D mode, you can move only on the "shadows" on the walls and flat objects. Shadows can be created by yourself through interaction with various objects in 3D mode. You need to use appropriate arrangement of their relation to one another and to light sources, so in the result you can move on them in the 2D mode.
The biggest downside is the length of the game - finishing it in almost 100% takes only 3-4h. Also, the "puzzles" are fairly simple. It's a pity that the authors failed to further develop the aforementioned theme, because the game had great potential. Nevertheless, I sincerely recommend Contrast, especially in some more accessible price.

There aren't that many games which would make me (or anyone) say "Wow that was cool" after they come to an end.
This one did it to me!
Contrast is an innovative game, taking some well known video-gaming genres and making from them something we haven't seen a lot lately (if at all), with its main downside of being very (!) short and perhaps a little rushed.
The main "punch" of Contrast is the you'd play around not only in your old-regular 3D world but also in the shadow world, yes, you'd step into a wall and become your own shadow.
Sounds simple, but fortunately Contrast doesn't just use the one and only gimmick it creates in order to try and make itself a good game, but also wraps it with some great graphics and sounds, interesting characters and a moving story in an exceptionally good noir atmosphere.
Too bad you can easily finish this game in about 3 hours, and if you like to take your time like myself, and explore every corner.. You may reach 6 hours. No more.
The game is also mostly not very challanging, and despite the interesting gameplay you can easily rush through the game, most of the time. And when you have some difficulties it would not necessarily be because of a challanging puzzle, but because some minor technical issue, as you may notice that the game and its mechanics aren't 100% polished.
I'm aware that the developers are new, independent and small company. But at some points I did wonder whether that's the reason for  those few and usually minor flaws in Contrast, or simply because it was too rushed.
Anyway, it doesn't hurt badly to my appreciation for this game.
Because of its great artistic values, because of it being new and unusual and yet so good and engaging, it may even be worth those 15 bucks, and I'd definitely recommend this game.

One of the best games I've played so far. Very original and fun, with some challenge to it.
To start off, the graphics are dated, but not bad at all. The motion scanner they used on the characters really bring them to life and play a big role in interrogations.
You play as a detective in the 1940's, and as such you examine crime scenes, find clues, and interogate suspects. It's all original and very interesting to do. Interrogation can oftentimes be tough, so I recommend taking your time finding all possible clues and examining the expressions of suspects very carefully. Trying to prove that a person is lying is particurlarly tricky, but very satisfying.
The game has chase scenes, both on foot and in cars. There are gun fights, which are fun but not particularly noteworthy. The city of LA is open-world, and you can find hidden cars and do some sightseeing.
It must be said, however, that the game is very mature, and you will often find brutal killings, blood, and naked victims. There are a lot of mature topics as well as some disturbing things, so I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone under 16.
Overall, the game is very fun and definitely worth your time and money.

Beautiful puzzler with a unique mechanic for in-game help.
You can do the whole game without the in-game help or a 3rd-party walkthrough if you want, but knowing that they're both available makes it less frustrating when you are struggling with something.
Stuck on where to place those cogs? Open the in-game "HandyManual" and turn to the Table of Contents, where you'll find a list of math problems... were there 7 rungs on the ladder and 3 windows? Multiply rungs by windows and add 37, turn to Page 58, get the clue to the cogs.
The whole game is made of pictures of 2D and 3D papercraft, so it has the feel of a pop-up children's picturebook. It's beautiful. Some of the little vignettes are cute, of solving the townspeople's problems. And you get a sense there's a history to the town that you're not fully being told (stay for the credits).
I played through the whole thing in <7 hours, not rushing particularly. There's not really any replayability, though I might go back and talk to some NPCs some more and look around a little.
Recommended for all fans of puzzle games, as well as people who want to like puzzle games but have been burned by puzzlers with nitpicky "do it exactly one non-intuitive way, and we won't help you" puzzles.
I'll almost certainly buy whatever this studio produces next. Lume and Lumino City were both great.

I never grew up playing point and click adventures game so naturally I don't carry any nostalgia for them.  I usually don't play too many of them because I personally find them quite difficult.  Many times puzzles require you make specific associations between different items or require you to find hidden details in the picturesque backgrounds.  Lumino City does a fabulous job separating itself from the crowd as an exemplary model of how a game in the genre should feel like.  A gorgeous art style, a wonderful sense of adventure, and cleverly designed puzzles make this game wonderfully endearing experience
The first thing that will immediately grab you're attention is the art style.  The game has a vibrant paper-craft look that just pops right out of the screen.  The world looks so real you feel like you could just reach right through the screen and touch it.  The is especially notice able during the little transitioning scenes during key parts of the story where you can see the world from different angles.  The natural abstraction of the paper-craft fits perfectly with the idea of a city built on a giant waterwheel.
There is a wonderful sense of adventure as you explore Lumino City.  On a journey to recuse your Granddad you'll have to traverse the city.  Each puzzle in the game offers two of three locales to explore.  The progression as you go from one area next fells very natural and offers a wonder sense of discovery.  This city has some wild architecture and you'll meet so very interesting indiviuals along the way.  You really never know what to expect and its always exciting to see whats around the next corner.
Well balanced puzzles is essential for this kind of game and Lumino City nails the balance superbly.  Yes, the puzzles can get quite difficult and many of the will really make you think.  However, patience is a virtue and the game gives you all the tools you'll need to figure out the solution.  Since you're limited a certain amount of space and resources for each puzzle you'll never feel too overwhelmed.  The variety is off the charts, every puzzle is unique and will have you thinking in a totally different way using a vast array of intellectual skills.
Playing this game is just incredibly rewarding.  The puzzles are all challenging yet they are all reasonable.  Every time you find the solution and progress to the next area its there is a wonderful sense of accomplishment.  Not only that but you're just dying to see whats next in this beautifully handcrafted world.  Not everybody will have the patience for these challenges but I highly recommend giving this game a shot.

Its challenging, detailed, and can get you at the edge of your seat at the drop of a hat. I highly advise this game if you are a fan of the old times, and if you're a history buff like me. I give L.A. Noire a 10/10.
